articleTitle: Detection Methodology for Multistage Voltage Sag Based on Residual Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The monitoring of voltage sags is a crucial prerequisite for mitigating their harmful effects. With the energy transition in power systems and the integration of a large number of distributed generations, multi-stage voltage sags (MSVS) are becoming increasingly common, causing more severe and profound impacts on the grid and users. Currently, there is a lack of effective description and detection methods for MSVS, posing challenges to their statistics, management, and prevention. Due to the varying residual voltages and multiple transition moments of MSVS, traditional methods struggle to effectively detect them. To address these difficulties, this study proposed a novel detection method based on residual analysis, tailored for the special characteristics of MSVS. First, relevant terms for MSVS were introduced, providing a foundation for the monitoring and management of MSVS. Secondly, a detection algorithm based on residual analysis is proposed, achieving accurate identification of MSVS and precise detection of their mutation moments. The effectiveness and accuracy were validated with data from a 10kV distribution network. The proposed method lays the foundation for improving the power quality of the existing energy transition system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Maximum Integration Capacity of Distributed Photovoltaic Considering Power Quality Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With a high proportion of distributed PV integration, the voltage and harmonic problem of the power system is further aggravated. If the integration capacity of distributed PV exceeds the actual hosting capacity of the distribution network, voltage over limit and harmonic pollution are caused. It has severe negative impacts on the security and operational efficiency of the distribution network, which may lead to instability of the power system. It is necessary to study the PV maximum integration capacity to guide the rational integration of distributed PV and guarantee a quality electricity supply for the power system. Therefore, a maximum PV capacity assessment method considering power quality constraints is proposed in this paper, which determines the capacity limit by establishing a model of a distributed PV integration system and taking harmonic voltage and harmonic current as constraints. Finally, the simulation with distributed PV integration is built by ETAP to verify the accuracy of the proposed PV maximum integration capacity evaluation method.

articleTitle: Synchrophasor-based Source Localization for Power Oscillations via IVMD-Energy Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With widespread deployments of phasor measurement units in power systems, the localization of power oscillations has become feasible via energy-based method. However, the performance of energy-based method greatly lies in extracting precise oscillation components. Therefore, the paper proposes an improved variational mode decomposition-based Energy (IVMDE) method. Initially, Fast Fourier Transform is employed for identification o f o scillation f requency, o ffering a reference for subsequent component extraction. The IVMD is then utilized to extract oscillation components from synchrophasor measurements, which are subsequently employed in computing IVMD-Energy for each branch. Moreover, the slope ratio of IVMD-Energy is employed as an indicator of the energy flow direction in the power system, auto-mating the process of determining the source of oscillations. The results of simulation using WECC 179 test case data verify the effectiveness of IVMDE method.

articleTitle: Use Cases for Power Quality Data Analysis: Case Study for the Estonian Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Recent developments, such as the increase in renewable energy sources or the large-scale introduction of electric vehicles, can have a significant impact on Power Quality. As a result, network operators are increasingly installing extensive measurement systems to closely monitor their networks. These systems generate vast amounts of data, which contains highly valuable information that is often underutilized. This paper presents a systematic overview of different use cases for Power Quality data analysis and their potential benefits for network operators. A case study on Estonian transmission system operator (TSO) measurements showcases the practical implementation of some use cases, namely compliance with planning levels, seasonal variations, and trend developments.

articleTitle: Analysis Method for Supraharmonics of Voltage Source Converters with Dual Dynamic Phasors
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual dynamic phasor analysis method for the supraharmonics (SHs) in voltage source converters (VSCs). With double Fourier transformation, a periodical signal with two different frequencies can be presented in frequency domain. Pulse width modulation (PWM) with modulation signals and carrier signals can be depicted as dual dynamic phasors (DDPs) defined by the double Fourier transformation. DDPs can be also transformed into dual dynamic phasor sequence components (DDPSCs) by symmetrical component method. With DDPs and DDPSCs, an analysis model of VSC can be developed as a state space equation, which can describe the switching dynamics and the SH interactions between ac and dc side. Simulations in different situations are applied to verify the correctness of the analysis model and some interesting findings are given in the paper.

articleTitle: A Fast Voltage Sag Evaluation Method of Distribution Systems with Inverter Interfaced Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The voltage sag caused by the fault may make the sensitive equipment trip and cause huge economic loss, so it is very valuable to study the voltage sag evaluation to prevent voltage sag. This paper presents a fast voltage sag evaluation method for an unbalanced distribution network with an inverter interface for distributed generators (IIDG). Rapid assessment of voltage sag needs to be based on accurate short-circuit current calculation. IIDG should operate following the low voltage ride-through (LVRT) requirement during the fault, which makes the fault current characteristics more complicated. In addition, the three-phase coupling components are difficult to decouple in unbalanced distribution systems. Therefore, the traditional symmetric component method cannot be applied in voltage sag evaluation in unbalanced systems with IIDG. In this paper, the short circuit calculation equivalent model of IIDG is analyzed. A rapid evaluation method of voltage sag based on block bordered diagonal form (BBDF) is proposed. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated by IEEE 13-node, 123-node, 478-node, and 954-node test systems. The results show that the proposed method has obvious advantages in computational efficiency

articleTitle: Power Flow Optimization of Bipolar DC Distribution Network Considering Voltage Unbalance
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The True Bipolar DC (TBDC) distribution network has the capability to supply two voltage levels. Because of high power supply reliability, large transmission capacity and easy access to distributed power supply and DC load, it has become a research focus in recent years. Firstly, the fundamental components and topological structure of the TBDC distribution network are analyzed to optimize power flow, minimize line loss, and reduce the imbalance between positive and negative pole voltages. Then, a power flow optimization model is proposed by modifying the droop coefficient of each DC/DC converter, adjusting the energy storage output, and controlling the load power. The model can absorb the distributed photovoltaic, adjust the voltage of each node to the allowable range, reduce the voltage imbalance between positive and negative poles, as well as decrease the overall line loss of the DC distribution network. Finally, A 5-node and a modified IEEE 69-node TBDC distribution network are built to validate the effectiveness and applicability of the optimization model proposed. The ultra-short term optimal dispatching simulation of the modified IEEE 14 node network is carried out to verify the superiority and energy-saving effect.

articleTitle: Research on Non-Intrusive Identification of Operating Status of Power Quality Management Device
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: SGCC of China has developed a monitoring system for power quality and various types of evaluation indicator systems. In this study, a non-intrusive method for identifying the operating status of power quality management devices has been introduced. The method uses a probabilistic neural network to classify evaluation indices. By comparing evaluation indices before and after the operation, the method can determine whether the management device is performing as expected. Additionally, for the purpose of practical applications, this study provides power quality evaluation indices and data preprocessing methods for status identification. The accuracy of the method has been validated using MATLAB to analyze real measurements of a 35kV STATCOM installed at a substation.

articleTitle: Power Quality in On-Board Grid of Passenger Trains
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Modern electric trains are equipped with single-phase electrical sockets powered by an on-board low-voltage converter. They enable the powering of the passenger’s private electronic loads. This paper contains the results of the voltage quality assessment on eight electric trains (seven powered by the use of standard electric traction and one electric drive railbus). The assessment took into account power interruptions, frequency, rms value, distortion (THD coefficient and higher harmonics), and the amplitude of voltage fluctuations. Measurements of the calculated quality measures have been performed during scheduled train runs in four European countries: Poland, Germany, France, and Switzerland. EN 50121-3-2 and associated standards were used to evaluate power quality.

articleTitle: Optimization Configuration Method for Voltage Sag Monitors Considering Photovoltaic Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) power sources has brought new problems to voltage sag in new power systems. Optimizing the configuration of voltage sag monitoring devices is an effective means to reduce monitoring costs. This article uses high-order Markov chains and Gaussian mixture models to probabilistic model PV power sources, improving the accuracy of PV probabilistic modeling. The calculation method for correcting residual voltage amplitude considering the low voltage ride through (LVRT) characteristics of PV is proposed. The optimization configuration method is based on the constraint that all system faults can be recorded by the monitoring device, and the optimization objective is to minimize the configuration cost of the monitoring devices. The obtained configuration scheme not only meets the economic requirements but also ensures that all voltage sags caused by faults in the system can trigger at least one monitoring device to record in power systems with PV access. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through simulation analysis using an IEEE30 node testing system.

articleTitle: Data-driven Voltage Sag Source Localization Based on Kernel Naive Bayesian Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low locating accuracy, data anomalies and missing in the extracted feature of the existing source localization methods, a data-driven voltage sag source localization is proposed based on multiple localization features and Kernel Naive Bayesian (KNB) classification. Firstly, in order to explore embedded information of the sag events, the causing mechanism of five type voltage sag is analyzed by simulation results, and seven kinds of localization features are extracted. These features include disturbance power and energy, impedance real polarity, system trajectory slope, current real-part polarity, and positive and negative sequence disturbance power. Then, considering that voltage sag source localization is actually a binary classification task, this paper adopts a simple and efficient kernel naive Bayesian classifier combined with multiple localization feature vectors to construct an upstream and downstream localization model of voltage sag sources for improving the accuracy and robustness of method. Finally, simulation verification is carried out in the IEEE33n ode system. The results show that, compared with common source localization methods, the proposed method has a high localization accuracy, as well as good reliably in locating various types of voltage sag sources when the feature data contains abnormal or missing data. It is applicable in complex practical applications.

articleTitle: Harmonic Source Modeling Method Based on VMD-DBSCAN
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Based on the existing research, this paper proposes a harmonic source modeling method based on VMD-DBSCAN for existing household multi-state harmonic source loads. First, this paper uses VMD-DBSCAN to identify the state of the harmonic source load, and then combines the identified state with the equivalent impedance parameters of the load to establish a harmonic source model. Finally, the simulation model data and private data set data are used to analyze and verify the proposed method. The experimental results show that the proposed method has the advantages of high identification accuracy and modeling accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Voltage Stabilization Strategy Based on Hierarchical Distributed Control for LVDC Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Compared to traditional alternating current (AC) power supply system, the low-voltage direct current (LVDC) system shows great superiority in simpler structure, lower power loss, and better compatibility with distributed generation. However, source and load fluctuations may cause system unstable. The DC-bus voltage stabilization is the key challenge in realizing DC system stability. Therefore, a voltage stabilization strategy can be designed for the existing hybrid energy storage system (HESS) composed of supercapacitor and battery, which is a promising solution for power balance. In this paper, a novel voltage stabilization strategy based on hierarchical distributed control for the LVDC supply system is proposed, which can allocate the power fluctuation to HESS without communication, recover the DC-bus voltage to rated value accurately, and achieve energy management in the LVDC system. Simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Influence of Superimposed Harmonic Current on Grounding Current in Metal Shielding Layer of 10kV Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: As new power systems rapidly advance, the influence of harmonic currents of power cables is becoming increasingly evident. For 10kV medium voltage three-core cables, the magnitude of the total grounding current is related to the currents on the three-phase cores. When harmonic currents of different frequencies are superimposed with AC on the cable cores, the magnitude of the grounding current increases relative to AC alone. This article provides an analytical calculation method for the total grounding current of cable metal sheath under the condition of AC superimposed harmonics based on electromagnetic field theory.

articleTitle: Exploring Daily Variation Patterns on Total Harmonic Distortion Long-Term Measurements in Traction Converter Stations using Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In Sweden, traction converter stations supply the traction system and deliver power to the trains. Those stations have the role of converting the 50 Hz public grid frequency to the railway operating frequency, which in Sweden is 16 ⅔ Hz. Measurements regarding harmonic parameters, including total harmonic distortion (THD), are imperative to keep the power quality in good performance and provide the operators with more information for investigation or compliance. This work proposes methods for assessing patterns on THD daily variation measurements in traction converter stations. For that, statistical analysis of data is explored together with a technique based on deep autoencoder (DAE). The methods are applied in measurements from five different traction converter stations, considering both the public and railway grid sides. The outcomes provide insights into the railway operation and distortion levels for long-term periods, also illustrating how different methodologies can be used for time-varying harmonic distortion, which can be deployed in any system with similar characteristics. The process brings up several good pieces of information and successfully finds patterns for daily variation in harmonic distortion. Such application can be extended to other measurements in electrified road systems, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, microgrids, wind parks, etc.

articleTitle: Research on Interactive Oscillation Suppression of Grid-forming VSC Grid-connected system
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The "double high" background presents new demands for grid-connected inverters, namely grid-forming capability and inertia support capability. virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology has rapidly developed to meet these demands. However, when there is a disturbance in the command power, interaction between VSG control loops can easily cause interactive oscillations, threatening the safe and stable operation of the new type system. Consequently, the improve the VSG is proposed to improve the dynamic response characteristics by using speed damping power high-pass feedback in active power-frequency control loop. Firstly, bode plots are applied to compare the transient and steady-state characteristics between traditional and improved VSG control methods. Secondly, the interaction of active power loops is analyzed using the relative gain array (RGA) principle. Finally, simulations are conducted to verify the proposed method for suppressing interactive oscillations, and which indicate that the improved method could well suppresses the interactive oscillation.

articleTitle: Interpolated Zero-padded FFT Algorithm for Harmonic Analysis Based on Zero-padded Window Function Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Fast Fourier transform (FFT) is commonly used in engineering for harmonic analysis due to relatively low computational complexity. However, FFT make sure that the length of the data must satisfy certain conditions, such as 2/3/4 or other inter powers. Aiming at the fact that the length of the data window is a non-integer power, an improved interpolated zero-padded FFT harmonic measurement algorithm is proposed. The core of the algorithm is to transform the interpolation correction of the zero-padded FFT into the fitting correction of the spectral response based on the zero-padded window function. 5-term maximum side lobe decay speed window is used to correct the data. The proposed algorithm is suitable for any zero-padded window function and avoids to derive a modified formula. Simulation and experimental results verify the effectiveness of the algorithm in harmonic analysis.

Author Keywords: 5-trem maximum side lobe decay speed window

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling of APFC-type Electric Vehicle Chargers in a Wide Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The number of electric vehicles (EVs) and charging equipment has been rapidly increasing in recent years. As a typical nonlinear load, their impact on the quality of electrical energy in the grid is manifested in a wide frequency domain. Focusing on Active Power Factor Correction (APFC) chargers for EVs, this study elaborates on the generation of harmonic currents from both high-frequency and low-frequency perspectives, combined with the two-stage charging process of electric vehicles. It derives the formula for the native emission of harmonic currents and establishes a dynamic model of current sources in a wide frequency domain. Finally, through the comparative analysis of simulation and theoretical results, the correctness of the modeling method proposed in this paper is validated.

articleTitle: Correction Method for SVG Loss Measurement Considering the Influence of Transformer Angular Difference
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Since the power factor angle is distributed around ±90° during SVG operation, the angular difference of the transformer has a significant impact on the SVG loss measurement. A power factor angular kernel density estimation-based correction technique for SVG loss measurement is presented as a solution to this issue. The method models the probability distribution using kernel density estimation by screening the base wave power factor angle of SVG inductive and capacitive specific power intervals. Based on the power factor angle corresponding to the time when the probability density is maximized, the angular difference of the transformer is calculated and compensated, thus improving the accuracy of the SVG loss measurement. Finally, the validity of the proposed method is verified through simulations as well as field cases. The results show that the proposed method can accurately correct the fixed phase angle error introduced by the transformer, and thus improve the accuracy of SVG intrinsic loss measurement.

articleTitle: Optimized Control Method Based on Implicit Arithmetic for Shunt Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The control strategy based on implicit arithmetic for active filter is proposed. The implicit arithmetic-based control strategy derives the duty cycle function of the bridge arms of each phase under the assumption that the grid current is sinusoidal, thus controlling the switching tubes on and off. It does not require a harmonic detection algorithm to achieve a better harmonic compensation effect. It is able to compensate the reactive power output so as to achieve a power factor close to 1. The main factor that makes this control strategy superior to other control methods is that it can achieve a good control effect in a relatively simple way. Finally, the control method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Impact of Sustained Supply Voltage on Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The widespread adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs), which increase electricity demand, has posed certain challenges for the electrical power system. Coupled with the elevated level of renewable energy penetration, distribution networks are encountering voltage regulation issues. This paper investigates the behaviour of EV chargers when exposed to rms voltage magnitudes across the allowable range through analysis of laboratory and field measurements of the electrical performance of several EV models and chargers, ranging from Level 1 to Level 3. The charger rms current, current total harmonic distortion (ITHD), displacement power factor (DPF), and power consumption have been measured. The data revealed that across the tested voltage range, the EV chargers primarily exhibited constant current (CC) behaviour, with some switching to constant power (CP) mode at higher voltage magnitudes. In addition, variation in supply voltage magnitude had no visible effects on the DPF, which remained close to unity, or ITHD. The outcomes of this study enable a more accurate understanding of EV load models, which aids the precision of power flow analysis, load management, and system planning.

articleTitle: Novel Harmonic Emission Limit Concept for Series-connected Distorting Installations Connected to Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The current technical standards for allocating harmonic emission limits in transmission systems do not consider series-connected distorting installations (like TCSC, HVDC links, etc.). This paper introduces a novel approach for the calculation of harmonic emission limits for series elements. The approach is developed based on the results of simulations of a test network with TCSCs connected in different lines, which showed that TCSCs have a considerable effect on the harmonic emission, and therefore series elements should be considered in the allocation process. Different global and local approaches for the harmonic emission limits allocation are proposed and applied exemplarily to the considered test network.

articleTitle: Intermittent Arc Fault Section Location in Power Distribution Network Using Distributed HFCT Disturbance Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Intermittent arcs in the distribution network have a random distribution and prominent high-frequency characteristics. This paper proposes innovatively using High-Frequency Current Transformers (HFCTs) installed distributedly in cable networks to capture waveforms of intermittent arc faults. Through real HFCT experiments, the paper validates the effectiveness of HFCT in capturing high-frequency arc waveforms. Building upon experimental sampling results, the paper employs empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and the Teager energy operator (TEO) to decompose the filtered arc transient disturbance waveforms through HFCT, and proposes a method for arc section location based on transient disturbance energy and phase comparison. The method is tested on an IEEE 34-node distribution network, demonstrating that the proposed method can effectively localize intermittent arc faults in underground distribution networks. This paper significantly extends the utility value of HFCTs, providing new insights and monitoring schemes for early fault detection in underground cable networks.

articleTitle: Fault Identification of Autotransformer Traction Network Based on Incremental Current Differential Angle Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A fault identification method for segmental autotransformer (AT) traction network is proposed, which can reduce the range of accidental power outage and improve the reliability of power supply. Firstly, based on the faulty and non-faulty current characteristics of the AT traction network, the incremental current differential angle (ICDA) relationship is derived for various fault types in each subsection. Furthermore, a fault identification method is proposed, which can identify the faulty subsection of the AT traction network as well as distinguish the fault types according to the ICDA variations of the contact wire and the negative feeder. Finally, a simulation model is established to analyze the correctness of the derivation of the ICDA relationship and verify the effectiveness of the proposed fault identification method.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of IEC 61000-4-30 Evolution in Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the continually increasing requirements for the performance and reliability of equipment in global power system, the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) is consistently updating the relevant standards so as to accommodate new technologies and face new challenges. IEC 61000-4-30 is an essential document on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC), with a focus on concepts of power quality and its measurement methods. Aiming to provide relevant engineers and professionals with an in-depth understanding of the latest standards, this paper compares and analyzes the significant differences between IEC 61000-4-30 Ed3 and IEC 61000-4-30:2015+AMD1:2021 CSV. While IEC 61000-4-30 Ed3 provides a comprehensive set of measurement methods for related parameters of power quality, including voltage, current, frequency, and their harmonics and flicker, IEC 61000-4-30:2015+AMD1:2021 CSV offers significant technical revisions based on Ed3, including the specifications for current measurement methods, the addition of measurement methods for rapid voltage changes (RVC), and the supplementation of measurement methods for conducted emissions in the 2 kHz to 150 kHz range. Through a comparative analysis of these two versions, we can comprehend the development of IEC standards and their significance in the application in the global power system better.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Ride through Analysis for the Connection of Photovoltaic Installations to the Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: An important indicator of the network is the ability to overcome faults, namely Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT). This paper analyzes the conditions imposed by the legislation in force, the implementation and verification of the fulfillment of the conditions for photovoltaic power plants. From the point of view of the transient regimes that appear in this type of plant, the fact that they do not have inertial generators can be considered that their operation is easier. An element that is still important and must be followed, is that in case of a short circuit, the power plant does not disconnect and has the ability to pass over the defect correctly eliminated by the protections.

articleTitle: Optimal Day-Ahead Power System Scheduling Considering Linearized Short-Circuit Current Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for short-circuit current suppression that considers both unit start-stop operations and line switching. By analyzing the physical relationship between the node admittance matrix and the node impedance matrix, as well as the physical significance of node self-impedance, we derive the relationship between line switching, unit start-stop operations, and short-circuit current. Subsequently, we propose a day-ahead optimal scheduling model that incorporates short-circuit current constraints, with the objective of minimizing raw material costs, environmental costs, start-stop costs of generating units, and short-circuit switching costs. Finally, we analyze the impact of this approach on the power quality of the system. The effectiveness and generality of the proposed model are validated using the IEEE 30-node system, and we present a day-ahead scheduling scheme that accounts for unit start-stop operations and line switching.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling and Sizing of Battery Energy Storage System in an Industrial Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This research aims to optimize an operation and economic efficiency of an industrial microgrid by focusing on two primary objectives: identifying the most cost-effective electricity, operating, and maintenance schedules, and determining the optimal battery size for industrial microgrid implementation. These objectives are set against the backdrop of challenges such as over-integration of renewable energy (RE) sources, which can lead to inefficiencies and reliability issues, and the need to enhance battery energy storage system (BESS) performance to ensure stability and responsiveness to demand fluctuations. Through rigorous analysis and optimization techniques, this study successfully addresses these problems by developing strategies that significantly reduce energy expenses for industrial facilities. The optimization outcomes demonstrate how strategic scheduling and sizing of a microgrid, and BESS can lead to more efficient use of renewables, minimizing reliance on the grid during peak demand periods. Consequently, the research contributes valuable insights into achieving economic and operational efficiency in industrial microgrid systems, promoting a sustainable and resilient energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Harmonic Management Trading Model Counting The Harmonic Management Aggregator
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Under the background of "dual-carbon" target, the harmonic exceedance problem is getting more and more serious, and PV inverters are homologous with APF topology, which can assist in power quality management and join the harmonic management market. This paper introduces the concept of harmonic management aggregator, which participates in the harmonic management trading market as a third party and performs unified scheduling for each PV inverter. With the goal of maximizing the interests of harmonic source users, harmonic management aggregators and PV power plants, a two-layer masterslave game optimization model with fundamental current constraints, harmonic current constraints and other constraints is set up and solved by using the improved particle swarm algorithm. Through the MATLAB and OpenDSS software model for joint simulation calculations, the simulation results show that the optimization model proposed in this paper harmonic management effect is obvious, all parties revenue optimization effect is significant.

articleTitle: Research on Novel Three-Level DC/DC Converter with Energy Transfer Function and Bipolar DC Voltage Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: DC microgrids with photovoltaics (PVs) and energy storage (ES) can achieve the maximum utilization of solar power. However, when PVs are connected to a bipolar DC microgrid, the mismatch of PV output power and load will cause the unbalance of the positive and the negative pole voltages. Focusing on such an issue, this paper proposes a control strategy based on a three-level DC/DC converter topology which can transfer energy with an additional inductance from the power surplus pole to the power shortage pole and then control ES to make up the gap. The operational principles under the normal states and the energy transfer states are analyzed in details. Finally, a model of bipolar DC microgrid with PVs and ES is built by PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results verify the effectiveness and the applicability of the topology and the control strategy. The transferred power is quantified comparatively from the micro and macro perspectives.

articleTitle: Assessment and Treatment of Voltage Sag Based on Electric-Process PIT
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Based on the strong correlation between petrochemical enterprises and the typical process parameters, an evaluation method combining traditional voltage tolerance curve with process immunity time based on process parameters was proposed. This method constructs a comprehensive evaluation index of safe operation of chemical plant after voltage sag, including electrical parameters and process parameters such as head and flow in the production process, which can realize sensitive identification of electrical parameter collapse and process index imbalance caused by voltage sag. Then, a circuit model is built according to the electrical parameters of a petrochemical enterprise, such as the circuit and the important sensitive load, and the typical sensitive load voltage sag is evaluated and treated. The results show that taking corresponding treatment measures based on the evaluation method of electric-process immune time curve can effectively enhance the stable operation ability of sensitive load and improve the power quality of petrochemical enterprises.

articleTitle: A Framework for Energy Management and Power Quality Monitoring in Institution Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Electricity management systems are becoming increasingly important for industries because energy plays a vital role in human progress and economic development. These systems help control energy use in buildings, with many now turning to renewable energy to save energy and improve efficiency. However, the growing use of electronic devices and renewable energy can sometimes cause issues like voltage imbalances and power quality problems due to energy conversion processes. Ensuring good power quality is crucial for a continuous and reliable electricity supply. By combining energy management systems with power quality monitoring, a comprehensive system can be created. This system, called the Energy Management and Power Quality Monitoring System (EMPQMS), uses Lyapunov modeling and Stockwell Transform to optimize energy management and detect power quality disturbances. Laboratory experiments and site measurements conducted in an institution building in UTM, Johor using MATLAB R2022b and FLUKE PQ analyzer help verify the reliability of EMPQMS. This system aims to offer innovative features for energy management that benefit all stakeholders.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Distribution System Harmonic Impedance and Impact on Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A recent collaboration between the TUD Dresden University of Technology and King’s College London explored the challenges associated with modeling the harmonic impedance of distribution systems and assessing its effects at higher voltage levels. Two network models, incorporating both transmission and distribution system representations, were utilized. For each model, different parameters were considered for sensitivity studies, and the harmonic impedance at the transmission level was computed for each scenario. The findings indicate that some of the parameters result in notable effects only locally, while others impact impedance at the transmission system buses. Common parameters that affect both networks are identified, and future work is outlined.

articleTitle: Identification of Equivalent Impedance Models of Downstream Networks for Harmonic Studies in Extra High Voltage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of modeling the frequency-dependent network impedance of downstream high voltage (HV) networks for accurate harmonic studies in extra high voltage (EHV) transmission systems. With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources, HVDC stations, and Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS), the accurate assessment of harmonic levels within transmission systems has become crucial. The paper proposes a two-step modeling process, beginning with the determination of frequency-dependent impedance characteristics by field measurements or detailed network simulations. These characteristics are then used to fit generic equivalent circuit (EC) models, allowing for the representation of a wide range of typical impedance characteristics. Challenges encountered in the application of this framework, such as the selection of circuit topologies and parameter estimation methods, are discussed. The paper concludes with a demonstration of the suitability of various circuit models and outlines future research directions.

articleTitle: A High-Performance and Low-Cost Power Quality Flexible Control Device Topology and Its Modulation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In order to realize the comprehensive optimization of converter efficiency, cost and other indicators, this paper proposes an active neutral-point-clamped (ANPC) converter based on heterogeneous hybrid half-bridge shunt output, referred to as hybrid ANPC (HANPC) converter. HANPC consists of a low frequency module and a fundamental frequency module based on Si IGBT devices and a high frequency module based on SiC MOSFET devices. Furthermore, the shunt compensation principle of the high frequency module and the low frequency module is introduced. The low frequency of the Si device compensates the large current, while the high frequency of the SiC device compensates the small current and improves the waveform quality of the output total current. Secondly, aiming at the optimal device loss, the sharing ratio and switching frequency of the high frequency module and the low frequency module are optimized, and the modulation strategy of HANPC is given. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed topology and modulation strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Topology Reconstruction of Fully Blind Power Distribution Networks Using Natural Transient Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Fully blind distribution networks lack topology and internal monitoring data, commonly found in poorly managed underdeveloped areas. This hampers network control and integration of distributed energy sources. Past researches relying on historical or internal node monitoring fail to address this issue directly. This paper propose a novel method utilizing natural transient disturbances. It extracts transient responses from edge nodes, establishing shared cable length arrays based on disturbance propagation. Numerical relationships within these arrays construct the backbone branch matrix. Further, unbranched variable-cross-section nodes are identified using second-order reflection distortion points of disturbances, reconstructing the complete topology. Testing on a real 10kV network confirms the method's effectiveness in topology reconstruction, while also providing cable lengths and cross-sectional areas for each branch. This method offers a potential solution to the new challenge of fully blind distribution network topology reconstruction.

articleTitle: Power Quality Disturbance Identification Based on Optimized VMD and CNN-BiGRU
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With non-linear loads connected to the power grid, the harmonics they generate can cause distortion in the current and voltage waveforms, interfering with the accelerated aging of equipment. To ensure the stability of the power system, improve energy efficiency, and optimize system operation, it is necessary to identify and address disturbances in electric power quality. In order to identify power quality disturbance efficiently and accurately, this paper proposes the chaotic Crayfish Optimization Algorithm (COA) to optimize two parameters of variational mode decomposition (VMD), and to extract and select nine time-domain indexes of the Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) of the minimum fitness function value index. The feature phasors are fed into the Convolutional Neural Network-Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-BiGRU) of multi-head attention mechanism (MHA) for perturbation identification. Using Matlab platform to simulate ten types of disturbances, the accuracy rate can reach 99.72%, which verifies the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Harmonic Distortion Assessment for an Offshore Wind Farm System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The offshore wind farm has become a growing focus in the renewable energy development and may cause significant harmonic distortion in power systems. Since each wind turbine can be regarded as a harmonic source, the accurate assessment of harmonic distortion produced by a wind farm is a crucial issue for the wind farm operation. When simulating harmonic sources, the model selections can substantially impact the calculated harmonic distortion results. Therefore, the accurate modeling of harmonic sources for the wind turbines becomes an indispensable issue. This paper aims to evaluate harmonic distortion in an offshore wind farm system under each wind turbine’s rated output. The study cases compare the differences in simulation results between the harmonic source based on the IEC 61000-3-6 and the DIgSILENT unbalanced phase correction (UPC) models. Then, the findings are reported to for harmonic assessment of an offshore wind farm.

articleTitle: Harmonic Source Modeling of AC Electric Arc Furnace Based on Mechanism-data Serial Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The paper proposed a harmonic source model for AC electric arc furnaces (EAF) based on mechanism-data serial drive. Firstly, a steady-state model of EAF based on energy empirical formulas was established, and an asymmetric nonlinear resistance Chua's circuit was used as a modulation signal to simulate the chaotic mechanism inside the EAF, thus establishing a practical simulation model of the EAF. Based on measured data, the empirical parameters of the simulation model can be obtained, which in turn a large amount of harmonic simulation data can be acquired. Finally, an EAF harmonic source model was established by mechanism-data serial drive. The results show that the harmonic source model based on mechanism-data serial drive has good accuracy, which can provide reference and foundation for studying the harmonic emission level of AC electric arc furnaces.

articleTitle: Research on Power Quality of Distributed Generation Connection to the Distribution Power Grid Considering the Influence of Harmonic Additional Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the increasing demand for improved power quality from users and the integration of numerous distributed power sources into the distribution power grid, the current synthetic evaluation methods for power quality fail to select appropriate indices based on the characteristics of the evaluation object. This limitation makes it challenging to apply these methods in scenarios involving distributed generation connected to the distribution power grid. Therefore, this paper analyzes the issues related to power quality arising from the connection of distributed generation to the distribution power grid. It constructs an evaluation index system specifically for assessing the power quality of distributed generation connections and proposes a power quality evaluation approach that considers the impact of harmonic additional losses. Combined with the CRITIC method with an improved Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), the synthetic weights are calculated using the TOPSIS method, allowing for a quantitative evaluation of the power quality associated with distributed generation connected to the distribution power grid. Finally, the proposed evaluation method is verified by an example. Combined with the actual power quality data, the method can effectively and accurately evaluate the power quality of the distributed power supply connected to the distribution power grid, which provides valuable guidance and reference for improving the power quality of the distributed power supply connected to the distribution power grid.

articleTitle: Harmonic Frequency Identification Method Based on Recording Data and Impedance Model
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the large-scale incorporation of power electronic equipment to new-type power systems, the content of high-frequency harmonics exhibits an increasing trend. The bandwidth and sampling frequency of the existing harmonic measurement devices are mainly designed for low-frequency harmonic measurement requirements, which may lead to high-frequency harmonic measurement distortion. In response to this issue, this paper proposes a harmonic frequency identification method based on recording data and impedance model. This method applies voltage and current recording data and network parameters to calculate the system impedance, respectively. The deviation between the calculated results is adopted to determine the harmonic frequency of measurement distortion. Additionally, the possible real harmonic frequency is calculated based on the principle of spectrum aliasing, and the system impedance at this frequency is recalculated to identify the real harmonic frequency. In the end, simulation and field cases analysis are used to validate the effectiveness of the suggested approach. The findings demonstrate that the suggested approach is capable of precisely identifying the real high-frequency harmonics in the case of spectrum aliasing.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Grid Reliability: Evaluating Machine Learning Algorithms for Fault Classification in Inverter-Based Generators Interconnection Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Through the transition of the energy matrix, which has resulted in a more significant share of renewable energy sources, there is a massive integration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) in Electrical Power Systems (EPS). This integration increases system complexity and affects power quality due to the unconventional fault contributions of IBRs. Therefore, in recent years, several researchers have studied the challenges of IBRs for conventional protection systems associated with EPS. This work addresses the complexity attributed to IBRs for the fault (short circuits) classification task in transmission lines connected to a wind farm. The study explores the potential of intelligent methods using machine learning algorithms based on decision trees and association rules through the WEKA (Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis) software. The results demonstrated the effectiveness of intelligent methods for classifying faults, with success rates exceeding 99%. However, it was found that the signal noise level significantly impacts the accuracy of the evaluated methods. Furthermore, some intelligent techniques have demonstrated the advantage of visibility into their decision-making, returning trees or rules with low complexity after training, which would facilitate the interpretation of this process by end users and its practical implementation.

articleTitle: Analysis Model of Adjustment Potential of Industrial Large Users Based on Data Set Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Industrial load is a key part of the new load management system. Analyzing the adjustable potential of large industrial users is of great significance to alleviating the contradiction between power supply and demand and improving the load management capacity of the new power system. Due to the large power consumption and regularity of industrial load, its adjustable potential is huge and it is one of the most ideal demand response resources. First, the main production equipment of large industrial users is modeled and analyzed. Then, based on the improved K-means clustering algorithm and combined with the industrial user regulation potential evaluation index system, the data set of large industrial users is reconstructed to obtain a high adjustable potential data set of large industrial users. Finally, considering the adjustable potential characteristics of users, a Self-Training-Bi-LSTM potential prediction model is established to obtain the adjustable potential range of large industrial users. The example results show that the proposed model can analyze the adjustable potential of typical equipment of large industrial users, and the stability and accuracy of the model are high.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis Based Characteristic Identification Method for Harmonic Source
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the increasing number of nonlinear loads and the prevalence of users with harmonic sources connected to the power grid, harmonic pollution at the public common connection point (PCC) is worsening. Current power quality monitoring systems cannot perform specialized monitoring for each user, making it challenging to identify the respective harmonic characteristics of multiple users on the feeder. Therefore, a characteristic identification method for harmonic source based on correlation analysis is proposed. Firstly, large-capacity industrial users are screened based on user capacity. Secondly, temporal features such as typical production cycles and switching moments of working conditions are characterized. Then the time series data of multi-user power and power quality monitoring data at PCC are segmented based on the changing point detection, and the correlation between power and monitoring indexes for each time period is calculated to obtain the power quality characteristic of harmonic users. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by the measured data.

articleTitle: Survey of Harmonic Emission Limits Utilization Based on Measurements in Medium Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper studies the utilization of harmonic emission limits based on measurements in medium voltage networks in Germany. Disturbance measurements carried out over one week at around 100 different sites, including medium voltage customers and downstream low voltage networks, provide a credible basis for the analysis. The analysis focuses on the utilization of emission limits based on the harmonic currents of disturbing installations and their contribution to the harmonic voltage distortion at the point of connection. The results allow a robust assessment of the efficiency of the harmonic management and can identify possible inconsistencies in the electromagnetic compatibility coordination. The results highlight the importance of holistic analysis considering both harmonic currents and voltages for the measurement-based compliance assessment.

articleTitle: A Novel Transformer-integrated Power Flow Controller of Distribution Network with Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: To address severe transformer overload from impact loads like electric vehicles and three-phase imbalance from high-power single-phase loads, a novel transformer-integrated power flow controller with hybrid energy storage system (HESS) is proposed. First, the topology of the novel controller is studied, and the energy transfer characteristics under two typical operating conditions are analyzed. Next, the power distribution method of HESS and the control strategy of the bidirectional DC/DC converter are analyzed. Additionally, a control strategy for the grid-tied converter considering HESS is proposed. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed scheme is verified by simulation. The results show that the proposed scheme can effectively cope with the complex working conditions in the distribution network, addressing issues such as three-phase imbalance mitigation, reactive power compensation, and dynamic capacity enhancement.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Modular Multilevel Co-Phase Traction Power Supply System with PV and HESS
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The reliable operation of the Modular Multilevel Co-Phase Power Supply Device (MM-CPD), as a key component of the Co-Phase Traction Power Supply System (CTPSS), is of paramount importance. However, the access of photovoltaic (PV) and hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) can change the port current of the MM-CPD and affect its reliability. Therefore, firstly, a day-ahead optimization model of the CTPSS is developed to minimize the traction substation's daily operating cost, and the compensation current of each phase of the MM-CPD is determined. Secondly, the reliability calculation model for MM-CPD is established according to the physical failure mechanism and reliability prediction manual. Finally, the impact of PV and HESS access on the reliability of the MM-CPD is analyzed with actual traction load data as an example, and its best redundancy configurations are determined to maximize the reliability of the device.

Author Keywords: Modular multilevel co-phase power supply device
photovoltaic and hybrid energy storage system

articleTitle: Influence of Battery Storage Systems on the Flicker and Harmonic Emission of Prosumer Households
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Battery storage systems are increasingly being used in households with renewable energy generation in order to optimize the exchange of electrical energy with the network. This raises the question of how such battery storage systems affect flicker emission due to the additional power dynamics. This paper examines the influence of two commercial battery storage systems on flicker and harmonic emission using reproducible laboratory experiments. The results show that both systems have a small, but significant influence on flicker emission. The causes of the behavior are analyzed and shown. These results contribute to the understanding of power quality challenges in the context of increasing distributeed power generation and prosumer households.

articleTitle: Dominant Harmonic Sources Identification Considering Variation Characteristics of Impedances under Multiple Network Operation States
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Harmonic sources in new power systems are characterized by wide distribution and interactive coupling. Due to the negative impact of harmonic measurement distortion and multi-source interaction, the existing methods are prone to misjudge the dominant harmonic source. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a dominant harmonic source identification method based on impedance variation characteristics under multiple network operation states. This method firstly changes network operation states by switching passive components such as reactive power compensation devices. Then the average rate of change of the equivalent harmonic impedance at the point of common connection under different network operation states is calculated, and thus the dominant harmonic source identification is carried out according to the level of impedance variations. Through simulation data and field case analysis, the results show that the proposed method can identify the dominant harmonic sources more accurately than the existing methods.

articleTitle: Algorithm for the Quantitative Assessment of Customer Economic Impacts of Voltage Dips and Interruptions
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper proposes simple generic algorithms that can be used to calculate the economic impacts of interruptions and voltage dips on customers. The proposed methodology is easy to apply and requires little data. The algorithm uses sag and financial data that are well researched and generally readily available in most modern electricity networks. The results allow network service providers, regulators and customers to make an estimate of the customer costs of voltage dips at an individual site or across an entire network. This outcomes presented in this paper may be applied to undertake cost-benefit analysis for voltage dip and interruption remediation works that may be proposed by networks owners or required by regulators.

articleTitle: Recommendations and Insights on the Performance of Conventional Fault Detection and Classification Methods Applied to Onshore Wind Farm Collectors
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of conventional fault detectors and classifiers when applied to diagnose faults in onshore wind farm collector systems. Two measurement sets are considered for the assessments: 1) a single measurement point on the collector transformers’ primary or 2) multiple measurements on the main collector busbars, assuming the faulty collector busbar is known. For the study, a system with a real-world topology for connecting IBRs to the grid was modeled using the PSCAD software. Several fault scenarios were represented with variations in fault type, resistance, inception angle, and location, along with varying the wind farm’s generation level. The studies provide recommendations on the best-performing conventional fault detection and classification methods when applied in onshore wind farm collector systems, besides sharing insights on the most appropriate measurement points for such tasks.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Storage Energy Management Collaborative Optimization Method for Improving Power Quality in Ship Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Aiming at the challenge that the traditional single energy storage scheme can hardly meet the power quality demand under complex working conditions, this paper proposes a multi-objective co-optimization technique grounded in the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) for hybrid energy storage in ship DC integrated power systems. In this paper, second-order filtering is adopted as the approach for handling energy administration. Next, developing a collaborative optimization framework that takes into account the interrelated aspects of capacity distribution and energy management tactics. Besides, the optimal filter coefficients and optimal energy storage capacity are solved by NSGA-II. Ultimately, the proposed method was evaluated through a simulation model, and the findings indicated that it not only curbs power fluctuations more effectively, but also enhances the quality of the ship’s electrical grid, diminishes the DC bus voltage variations, and ensures that the system’s investment costs are kept to a minimum.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control for Unbalance and Voltage Fluctuation in the Distribution Station Area
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the development of renewable energy, the proportion of photovoltaic power generation in the distribution station area is increasing. Combined with the existence of a large number of single-phase loads, the voltage fluctuation and three-phase unbalance in the station area are becoming more serious. Considering the flexibility and wide applicability of governance, this paper proposes a coordinated control using single-phase energy storage to solve two problems. Firstly, based on the principle of energy storage capacity distribution, this paper derives the capacity required to control three-phase unbalance and voltage fluctuation respectively, and sets the energy storage input power accordingly. Secondly, considering the influence of energy storage capacity constraints on the governance effect, the governance schemes under sufficient and insufficient capacity are proposed respectively. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed comprehensive treatment scheme is verified by Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Synchronous Generator Harmonic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In order to predict voltage distortion in stand-alone synchronous generator supplied systems, accurate harmonic models of the machine are required. In an industrial context, often simplified models based on the inverse sequence and subtransient reactance are used. However, if the full machine is considered, a process known as frequency conversion occurs. In this paper, the deviation between the voltage distortion predicted through simplified models and frequency conversion is derived. Using these expressions, the error made through the simplified models is calculated for commercial machines with varying power ratings. Finally, the error calculation is applied to a 250kVA machine and evaluated through simulation. Based on the results, the negative sequence reactance yields the most reliable results, with an important reduction in the error for high power machines. However, for machines with a high subtransient saliency, the use of simplified models will result in significant errors.

articleTitle: Technologies for Protection and Efficient Capacity Utilization of Emergency Power Supply Vehicles Based on Multi-Mode Negative Sequence Compensation Control
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Currently, diesel generators are widely utilized in most emergency power supply vehicles due to their convenience and reliability. However, with the continuous development of people’s lives, the requirements for power quality of various loads have been increasing significantly, thus making power quality issues during emergency power supply particularly important. In response to the characteristic of diesel generators requiring a relatively longer start-up time, this paper proposes a multi-mode negative sequence compensation method applicable under different operating conditions of emergency power supply vehicles, along with a switching control method between these modes. This approach ensures that negative sequence compensation can be effectively carried out both when the diesel generator is not connected to the grid and when it is already connected. Moreover, during the transition between these two operating states of the diesel generator, this method enables smooth switching, thereby reducing the impact and oscillation caused by the generator’s connection to the system.

articleTitle: Harmonic Current Probabilistic Modeling Based on K-Fold Cross-Validation Kernel Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In the construction of the new energy system, the new power system's "double high" characteristics bring harmonic pollution to the power grid. Meanwhile, due to the different habits of power users and new energy generation affected by some uncertainties such as weather, randomness needs to be taken into account in the harmonic assessment, and the probabilistic model is an effective method to characterize the harmonic distribution. In this paper, a kernel density estimation model with bandwidth selection by the k-fold cross-validation method is proposed for estimating the probability density of harmonic currents. The efficacy of the proposed model is assessed through a conventional kernel density estimation method with a rule-of-thumb bandwidth selection. All models are tested using the coefficient of determination, mean absolute error, and root mean square error. The results show the proposed models perform better in assessing the probability density of harmonic currents for residential and commercial loads.

articleTitle: Improved Online Insulation Identification of Cable in DFIG-Based Offshore Wind Farm based on Harmonic Resonance Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Currently, DFIG-Based offshore wind farm is mainly connected to the power grid via AC cables, and online identification of cable insulation condition (CIC) is crucial for the safe delivery of wind power. A method has been proposed to estimate the CIC based on resonance frequency analysis, but it is difficult to be applied effectively because it cannot take into account the influence of the power grid harmonic impedance on the resonance frequency. As a result, this paper improves the methed by adding prior information through harmonic impedance estimation. Firstly, the harmonic impedance of the power grid is estimated online by using harmonic measurements at the point of common coupling (PCC) of the wind farm and grid, and is used as prior information for the CIC identification, then the relationship between the resonance frequency of the wind farm system and the insulation condition is established, and finally the CIC is determined according to the measured resonance frequency. Simulation case verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: ACVT Harmonic Recovery Method Based on Deconvolution and Local Least 2-Norm Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A harmonic voltage recovery method for Capacitive Voltage Transformer (CVT) based on deconvolution and local least 2-norm regression is proposed. The proposed method takes advantage of the periodic consistency of CVT’s primary and second side voltage. It uses deconvolution and local least square norm regression methods, respectively, under periodic and aperiodic conditions to calculate the first side voltage signals of CVT, which can avoid the influence of aperiodic sampling on the deconvolution method and reduce the cumulative error. Simulation results show that the proposed method can accurately recover steady harmonic voltage, harmonic amplification voltage, transient overvoltage, and other aperiodic voltages.

articleTitle: Variability of Power Generation in Small Photovoltaic Installations
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) installations convert the energy of optical radiation into electrical energy. The power of optical radiation reaching the Earth’s surface varies. Therefore, the electricity produced by photovoltaic installations also changes. Some of the changes are deterministic (annual and daily changes in the position of the Sun) and the rest are stochastic (obscuring by clouds, vegetation, birds, planes, etc.). The variability of optical radiation causes unpredictable changes in the generated power that is fed into the power grid. The paper describes examples of variability of power generated in small photovoltaic installations located in Poznan. The upper limit of power variability has been determined and compared with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Upstream and Downstream Localization of Voltage Sag Source Based on Downstream Equivalent Fault Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Voltage sags cause significant economic losses in people's daily lives, making it particularly important to pinpoint the location of the disturbance source to clarify the responsibilities of both upstream and downstream parties. Most current methods do not account for the presence of distributed generation (DG) on the user side, leading to less-than-ideal accuracy. This paper proposes a method for voltage sag source location based on downstream equivalent fault distance, which can achieve upstream and downstream localization of voltage sag source in distribution networks with DG. The method first involves identifying the equivalent parameters of the system's three-sequence network, then calculating the equivalent fault distance based on the identified fault type, and finally determining the relative position of the disturbance source based on the equivalent fault distance. Testing and analysis using the improved IEEE 33 system demonstrated high localization accuracy, validating the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Load Modeling and Analysis Considering the Impact of Microgrid Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A typical microgrid simulation platform with multiple distributed power sources has been constructed using various micro power source models that have already been built. Considering the support issues of internal voltage and frequency in the microgrid when disturbed, a PQ-Vf control strategy based on the voltage source inverter (VSI) has been established to ensure its stable operation. By using a comprehensive load model of induction motors plus constant impedance, the impact of microgrid access on the load model under different output conditions of micro power sources has been analyzed. This provides a beneficial exploration for load modeling and analysis considering the impact of microgrid integration.

articleTitle: A Novel Optimization Model for Harmonic Mitigation Based on Residual Capacity of Photovoltaic Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In the distribution network, the existence of harmonic sources will lead to the warping of current and voltage waveform, affecting the stability of power system and the correct functioning of equipment. In this paper, a novel optimization model for harmonic mitigation is proposed, which utilizes residual capacity of photovoltaic inverters after active grid connection to generate harmonic compensation currents. The model is solved by particle swarm optimization algorithm. The simulation results prove that optimization model proposed in this paper shows great robustness and effectiveness, which is able to achieve harmonic mitigation at all nodes when facing different harmonic exceedances and can reduce the average value of total harmonic distortion of voltage by up to 11.59%. This also provides theoretical support for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Geometric-based Power-Free Approach for Current Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Traditional methods for current compensation in power systems and electrical circuits have heavily relied on ad hoc defined power concepts. This paper introduces a novel, power-free approach to both active and passive current compensation based on vector projection and rejection principles. The proposed method leverages vector geometric algebra as a robust mathematical framework, providing a clear and intuitive way to perform these operations in electrical systems. This approach simplifies the understanding and computation of circuit compensation, offering a unified method applicable to both single-phase and multiphase systems, in time and frequency domains. The main advantage is the complete avoidance of power definitions in the compensation process, focusing instead on the geometric relationships between voltage and current vectors. The paper develops the theoretical foundation and mathematical formulation of this power-free approach, demonstrating its versatility in handling various electrical scenarios, including non-sinusoidal and unbalanced conditions. By providing a geometric interpretation of current components, this novel approach offers a promising alternative to traditional power-based methods, laying the groundwork for more intuitive and efficient compensation system design in electrical circuits and power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Suppression Strategy of SVG Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: As AC submarine cables are adopted to connect offshore wind farms to the onshore power grid, severe harmonic problems and the deterioration of power quality may be induced. To address the issue of excessive harmonics in the offshore wind farms, this paper applies the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) to static var generators (SVG) for harmonic suppression. Firstly, the model of SVG is established, and the harmonic propagation mechanism is analyzed. Secondly, the SVG voltage outer loop controller is designed based on the ADRC. On this basis, the system transfer function model is deduced, and the operational stability and harmonic suppression capability of ADRC are theoretically studied by using the frequency domain characteristic curve. Finally, the MATLAB/Simulink model of Jiangsu's offshore wind power plant is built to verify the effect of ADRC strategy on harmonic suppression. Simulative results show that the ADRC can effectively suppress the harmonics occurred in offshore wind farms, and the suppression performance is not affected by the operating conditions, and has strong robustness.

articleTitle: Optimization and Control Strategies for Stochastic Power Quality of Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: To solve power quality problems in distribution networks, this paper presents a distributed generation siting and capacity determination method. The methodology aims to minimize network losses, reduce the total harmonic distortion rate of voltage (THDV), and take into account load and power supply uncertainties. A probabilistic optimization solution algorithm that combines a traceless variation method and a traversal optimization algorithm is proposed, which greatly reduces the computational effort. Simulations are performed to validate it using an IEEE-69 node system. It is demonstrated that this proposed method improves the power quality by significantly reducing network losses.

articleTitle: Multi-party Collaborative Participation in the New-Quality Industrial Park's High-Quality and Cost-Effective Electricity Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In the pursuit of enhancing quality and efficiency, new-quality industrial users extensively employ Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Adjustable Speed Drivers (ASDs), and AC-Contactors (ACCs), which are sensitive to voltage sags in the production process. Voltage sags can lead to malfunctions, shutdowns, or abnormal operations of these sensitive devices, causing significant economic losses to users. New-quality industrial users are greatly troubled by voltage sags and have a strong demand for high-quality electricity.
