Currently, users often obtain high-quality electricity by configuring customized power equipment, but the high cost of purchasing such equipment increases production costs, leaving users in a dilemma. To address this issue, this paper proposes a high-quality and reasonably priced electricity strategy for new-quality industrial parks that takes into account the game relationship and reasonable cost-sharing among multiple parties. By introducing governments and third-party financial institutions to become cooperative entities sharing costs and benefits with users, the strategy aims to promote the development of high-quality electricity in new-quality industrial parks and achieve a quality-price balance.

articleTitle: DC Microgrid Ripple Detection Algorithm Based on SGMD-HT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In this paper, a ripple parameter measurement method based on the combination of Adaptive Sim Geometric Modal Decomposition and Hilbert Transform (ASGMD-HT) is proposed. It is applicable to the problem that ripples are difficult to be extracted in strong noise environments. First, the reconstructed trajectory matrix is constructed based on the Hamiltonian matrix with Sin QR decomposition, and the initial Sin geometry components are obtained by combining the Sin geometry similarity transform. Second, the initial Sin geometry components are fitted according to the similarity criterion and the residual components are calculated, and then the trajectory matrix is constructed based on the residual components. Then, the above operations are repeated until the iteration termination condition is satisfied to obtain the final mutually independent ripple components. Finally, the ripple parameters are extracted by Hilbert transform. The analysis results of simulation and measured data show that this method can accurately detect ripples under strong noise conditions.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Clustering Method for Phase Identification in Low Voltage Distribution Networks Based on Voltage Monitoring Data
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Acquiring the phase connection information of low-voltage distribution networks (LVDNs) is of paramount importance for power utility to achieve fine-grained operation of LVDNs. This paper presents a hierarchical clustering-based approach for phase identification in LVDNs, leveraging the voltage monitoring data from the advanced measurement infrastructures (AMIs). Firstly, principal component analysis (PCA) is employed to extract salient features from monitoring data. Secondly, a hierarchical clustering algorithm is applied to group the customers into various phase connectivity clusters based on salient features. Finally, the algorithm is applied on a real LVDN in Guangdong province, China, demonstrating an accuracy exceeding 90% for the phase identification task.

articleTitle: Dynamic Retail Pricing Model For Electricity Retailers Considering Power Quality Demand
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Dynamic pricing is conducive to the regulation of flexible resources in the distribution network, but the traditional dynamic pricing model does not take into account the power quality demand of power users. Connecting power quality with the dynamic pricing model can economically drive market participants to place a high priority on power quality. This study constructs a dynamic retail pricing model for power electricity retailers that considers the power quality demand. It is based on the power quality level of consumers and the demand response mechanism. The deep reinforcement learning algorithm is used to solve the model. The experiment shows that the model can effectively regulate the peak-valley difference of load demand in the face of electricity customers with different power quality levels. Moreover, the model provides theoretical and practical basis for the power purchasing company to formulate dynamic real-time retail tariffs and power quality service fees.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Volt-Var Optimization Considering Operation Cost of OLTC in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Frequent voltage fluctuations caused by the increasing penetration of renewable resources pose many challenges to distribution systems, which burdens the operation and maintenance cost of the regulated devices. The conventional methods of Volt-Var Optimization (VVO) regard the real power losses and voltage variation as the objectives. However, the ignorance of the operation cost of transformers degrades the efficiency and the economic performance of the distribution networks. This work engages the operation cost with the objectives. To overcome the non-convexity caused by the nature of power flow calculation, a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to address the multiple-objectives problem. The proposed approach is validated in a modified 33-bus network. The results illustrate the proposed method can achieve losses reduction, voltage regulation and economic operation of the distribution networks.

articleTitle: Harmonic Indices Prediction of LED Lamps Based on Voltage-Dependent Optimized Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Besides the driver circuit structure, the distortion of the applied voltages plays the main role in the field of Power Quality (PQ) emissions associated with power electronic devices, specifically Light Emitting Diode (LED) lamps. Thus, a total of 17 distinct voltage waveforms generated by programmable power supply are applied on samples of 8 LED lamps that have the same circuit topologies and the same wattage. These lamps are collected from different manufacturers within the European Union (EU) markets. This paper aims to analyze the current distortion behavior exhibited by each lamp during various applied voltages, with the ultimate objective of developing Machine Learning (ML) models capable of predicting specific harmonic indices. To assess the effectiveness of the optimized proposed models, namely Deep Neural Network (DNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), three distinct scenarios are created using varying data set split ratios.

articleTitle: AC Voltage Compensation and DC Voltage Balance on Cascaded H-bridge Converter for Dynamic Voltage Restorer
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: For sensitive loads in distribution network, voltage sag is a major power quality (PQ) problem, and the dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) is an effective device to solve this problem. This paper introduces a high-voltage direct-connected DVR based on a cascaded H-bridge multilevel converter. The dq-axis decoupling control scheme is developed for DVR AC voltage compensation, and carrier phase shifted pulse width modulation (CPSPWM) with voltage offset injection algorithm is applied for DC capacitor voltage balance of the multilevel converter. Finally, the proposed DVR is modeled and simulated by MATLAB/SIMULINK, and the feasibility of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: A Capacitor Switching Disturbance Detection Method Based on Voltage Differential Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: As the scale of power systems continues to expand, it is often necessary to switch capacitors to ensure the normal operation of the distribution network. However, there is currently no efficient, simple, and accurate method to detect transient disturbances caused by capacitor switching. This paper proposes a capacitor switching disturbance detection method based on voltage differential waveforms. First, voltage transient disturbances are detected for further analysis. Second, the voltage transient components are extracted, and a discrete Fourier transform (DFT) is performed on the data between the disturbance start and end points. The result of the DFT is the spectrum of the transient components, where the frequency corresponding to the highest spectral component is referred to as the dominant frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>. If f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> lies between 300 Hz and 1000 Hz, the transient disturbance is identified as caused by capacitor switching. Finally, the method is validated using an IEEE 30-bus system network as an example, with results consistent with both simulation and theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Harmonic Power Flow Calculation Method Based on VSC AC/DC Harmonic Interaction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Harmonics on both the AC and DC sides of the Voltage Source Converter (VSC) interact with each other. This paper introduces a convenient approach for calculating harmonic distribution of the power grid. Initially, employing the principles of bilateral Fourier series theory, a mathematical representation of the VSC's switching function is developed. Subsequently, a VSC harmonic source model that takes the influence of DC side harmonics into account is built by analyzing the interaction between the AC and DC harmonics. Furthermore, a simulation framework for the VSC is developed on the Matlab/Simulink environment to verify the accuracy of the suggested harmonic source model. Lastly, a practical harmonic power flow computation method depending on the suggested model is expounded. The computation method's viability is confirmed in the IEEE-57 bus network.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Ride-Through of A Direct-Series DSSC With Fault Current Limiting Function
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Direct-series distributed static synchronous series compensator (DSSC), when the controlled line short-circuit fault occurs, its core component converter is affected by the fault current, resulting in the DSSC out of operation, which may further deteriorate the stability of the system. In this paper, a direct-series DSSC with short-circuit limiting function (DSSC- FCL) topology is proposed, and its working principle is analyzed in detail, the parameter design principle of DSSC-FCL is given, and a fault ride-through strategy based on DSSC-FCL is proposed. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed direct-series DSSC-FCL has the power flow control function under normal working conditions. In the event of a fault in the AC system, the fault ride-through strategy proposed in this paper can effectively suppress the AC current and DC capacitor current of the device, protecting the direct-series DSSC from the impact of large short-circuit currents in the system. Additionally, after the fault is cleared, the strategy shortens the device's response time, thereby increasing the reliability and operational efficiency of the device.

Author Keywords: Direct-series distributed static synchronous series compensator

articleTitle: The Effect on Commutation Failure of Large Capacity HVDC Receiving Terminal With Excitation System of the Flexibility Modification Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper establishes the excitation structure and model for a flexibility-modified generator and derives the mathematical mechanism for calculating the rotating reactive power of a synchronous generator. By creating a PSCAD simulation environment at the HVDC load center terminal, the corresponding extreme grid potential during an unsuccessful commutation of the HVDC converter station is identified. Using a detailed excitation system model of the synchronous generator within the simulation, the support provided by the flexibility-modified generator's excitation structure during the unsuccessful commutation at the load center is demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Virtual Impedance-Based Controllably Inductive Power Filtering System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: To overcome the limitations of conventional inductive power filtering as a passive filtering approach, in this paper, an adaptive virtual impedance-based controllably inductive power filtering system (AVI-CIPFS) is proposed. This system consists of an inductive filtering transformer, an LC-filter bank, and an active inverter. Assisted by the multi-objective control strategies developed, it can dampen the resonance between passive filters and grid-side impedance, manipulate power factor, and perform multiple harmonic mitigation simultaneously. In addition, using the quasi-PR controller with frequency division detection, it also removes the coupling between active and reactive components in the dq0 frame, greatly reducing the steady-state current tracking errors. Experimental results demonstrate the practicality of this proposal.

articleTitle: Intelligent Flexible Control Device and Technology for Distributed PV
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) utilizes renewable energy sources for power generation, offering advantages such as carbon emission reduction and environmental friendliness. When distributed PV power exceeds the regional load consumption limits, it may lead to the issue that the reverse power flow exceeds the rated capacity of transformers and distribution feeders. This could result in abnormal operation of power equipment and power quality issues. Since these situations have frequently occurred in some regions, this paper proposes two developed devices and a specific implementation method to monitor, calculate and control distributed PV systems in real-time. These devices and systems have been widely applied. The conclusion of practice is that if the friendly interaction between distributed PV and the power grid can be achieved, the large-scale power outages under the extreme situations can be prevented.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks Based Power Quality Data Generation Method and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The construction of new power systems with more new energy resources connected to the power grid may lead to more power quality problems. In this paper, generative adversarial networks (GANs) method was used to process power quality data restoration. Firstly, the power quality data missing problem was elaborated and the feasibility of GAN in the application of power quality data generation was analyzed. Secondly, the GAN model for power quality data was constructed and the loss function was detail structured to improve the data generation accuracy and enhance the performance of missing data generation, which the processing procedure includes two-dimensional mapping conversion, greyscaling processing, data feature extraction, generative adversarial data training and calibration. Finally, F-test was conducted to verify the effectiveness of the method through experiments on repairing real power quality data.

articleTitle: A Virtual Phase Current Regulation Strategy to Mitigate Reactive Power Oscillation for Three-Phase Grid-Tied Inverter under Unbalanced Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A three-phase, three-wire grid-tied inverter, when operating under unbalanced voltages with traditional control strategies, inevitably injects the reactive power oscillating at twice the utility frequency. To mitigate or eliminate the reactive power oscillation, this paper proposes a virtual phase current regulation (VPCR) based strategy that is effective and easy to implement by incorporating a current feedback gain. The VPCR-based mitigation strategy can be activated in either the sagging or normal phases, with the former showing better performance, as demonstrated by the modeling of instantaneous power theory under the VPCR strategy. Subsequently, the proposed strategy is implemented in the simulation, effectively validating the proposed concepts and analysis.

articleTitle: Optimized Dispatch Strategy for a Hydropower-Wind- Solar-Storage Complementary System under Extreme Drought Conditions with Shiftable Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the intensification of global climate change, extreme weather conditions pose significant challenges to the stability of power systems. The multi-energy complementary system, integrating hydropower, photovoltaics, wind power, and energy storage, known as the hydro-wind-solar-storage complementary system (HWSSCS), has the potential to enhance the system's ability to accommodate fluctuations in renewable energy through the peak-shaving and frequency-regulation functions of hydropower. However, under extreme drought conditions, hydropower generation capacity is constrained, significantly increasing the complexity of system operation. In this paper, a short-term optimization scheduling model for HWSSCS, incorporating shiftable loads, is constructed to analyze scheduling strategies under drought scenarios and to investigate the impact of shiftable loads on the system's supply-demand balance. The results indicate that the integration of shiftable loads effectively alleviates power supply pressure during peak load periods, reduces load gaps and curtailment, and enhances the robustness and operational flexibility of the system.

articleTitle: A method for analyzing the stability of inverter-dominated microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the "carbon peak" and "carbon neutrality" strategy, the distributed power sources are steadily increasing, leading to the emergence of microgrids dominated by distributed power sources. This paper proposes a for analyzing the stability of inverter-dominated microgrids. Firstly, the microgrids’ small signal analysis model is established, including critical components such as synchronous generator sets, inverters. By incorporating these elements, the model can accurately represent the dynamic behavior of the microgrid under various operating conditions. The Nyquist stability criterion is then employed to systematically analyze the impact factors of the microgrids’ stability, including control bandwidth of current-loop, PLL, dc-voltage-loop. The analysis indicates that an increase in distributed power generation reduces the system's stability margin, and adjust the control parameter can improve the stability characteristics. Finally, simulation analysis is conducted to verify the conclusions derived from the analysis.

articleTitle: Supraharmonics Mitigation Strategy of Rolling Mill Converter Clusters Considering High-frequency Circulating Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The integration of fully-controlled rolling mill converter clusters leads to an increase in the supraharmonics content of the distribution networks. Each rolling mill converter operates in different states with inconsistent carrier phases, resulting in serious high-frequency circulating currents(HFCC) between converters. Moreover, existing carrier phase-shifting strategies fail to mitigate supraharmonics and HFCC comprehensively. Within this context, this article proposes a supraharmonics mitigation strategy considering HFCC for rolling mill converter clusters. This strategy is founded on the tenet of random carrier frequency pulsation width modulation. According to the correlation between carrier frequency randomness and supraharmonics amplitude and phase randomness, the supraharmonic emission characteristics are modeled, and the HFCC model is constructed. The interactive coupling mechanism of supraharmonics of converter clusters under random carrier frequency is analyzed. Additionally, the carrier frequency is randomly changed so that switching frequency dominated harmonics are not formed between converters. Consequently, the generation of HFCC is suppressed. Finally, real case studies are conducted to validate the efficacy of the proposed means. The outcomes indicate that the mitigation rates of grid-side supraharmonics and HFCC are more than 88% and 85%, respectively, indicating satisfactory comprehensive mitigation performance.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on Power Quality Assessment Index System Oriented to Application Value
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the development of economy and technology, the issue of power quality (PQ) is attracting increasing attention. However, the indices and results obtained by the existing PQ assessment methods are not intuitive, and it is difficult for non-professionals like social investors and power users to understand the impact of PQ on themselves. In this paper, a PQ assessment index system for social investors, power grids, and power users is proposed. The professional PQ indices are converted into easily understandable indices for public, such as economic index. What’s more, case studies are given to make the indices more intuitive.

articleTitle: Norton Based Modelling Techniques for Assessing the Harmonic Emissions of Inverter Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The proliferation of Inverter Based Resources (IBRs) connected to high voltage (HV) transmission networks can have detrimental impacts on waveform distortion. This is caused by the power electronic interface, with voltage source converter (VSC) technology being by far the most prevalent. As such, proper emission models, which can account for the non-linear operation of VSCs, must be developed and investigated for the assessment of harmonic distortion in HV networks. Norton based modelling techniques for assessing the harmonic emissions of inverter base resources are compared in this paper. Some recalls about the frequency domain modelling of IBRs are firstly given. Then, Monte Carlo simulations on two case-studies based on a PV plant and a Type IV wind turbine show quantitatively the performances of four Norton based models characterised by different levels of approximation.

articleTitle: Lightweight Power Quality Monitoring Based on Improved Least Squares State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In order to realize the lightweight configuration of Power Quality Monitors (PQM), an improved weighted least squares state estimation method is proposed, and the PQM configured with the monitoring reach area analysis method is used to realize the harmonic voltage monitoring. The method realizes nodal voltage sag and harmonic voltage observation with the configuration scheme of less PQM. Firstly, based on the voltage sag value at the monitoring point when the fault occurs, the monitoring reach area of voltage sag is established to realize the configuration of voltage sag PQM. Secondly, according to the accuracy difference of measured data, the weight factors of state estimation of data with different precision are set. Finally, combined with the measured values of harmonic voltage, active power and reactive power, the improved weighted least squares method is used to estimate the harmonic state and realize the observable analysis of harmonic voltage. The proposed method is simulated and verified by the IEEE 14-bus system. The results show that the proposed method can realize the observable analysis of voltage sag and harmonic voltage based on limited measuring devices, and realize the lightweight configuration of PQM.

articleTitle: Robust Optimal Power Flow for Distuibution Network Based on Holomorphic Embedding Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper proposes a more robust optimal power flow algorithm (ROPF) to address the issue of optimal power flow solutions being more likely to be attracted to inoperable solutions in new power systems. Firstly, the holomorphic embedding power flow algorithm (HEM) and particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) are decoupled and reconstructed within the algorithm to achieve cross solving of the distribution network OPF problem. Secondly, based on the consideration of voltage quality and economic operation in the distribution network, a multi-objective optimization model was established with the system loss and voltage deviation rate as objective functions, and the flexible resource operation status of the distribution network as decision variables; Finally, using the ROPF to conduct simulation experiments on IEEE-33 system and compare the results with the OPF algorithm based on the NR method. The results indicate the ROPF has better robustness and practicality.

articleTitle: Lightweight Data Fusion Acquisition Method Based on Non-Sinusoidal Power Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The distribution systems with photovoltaic (PV) integration have limited capacity to accommodate power quality measurement devices, which poses challenges in data acquisition and characterization of power quality disturbances. In this paper, a lightweight method for power quality data fusion acquisition based on the non-sinusoidal power feature is proposed. Firstly, the non-sinusoidal power theory is introduced, which separates the voltage and current components at harmonic and fundamental frequencies. Secondly, a lightweight data fusion acquisition method based on the non-sinusoidal power system is proposed. Through defining multiple non-sinusoidal power indicators, the power quality data feature fusion indicator system is proposed. Accordingly, the fusion relationship between non-sinusoidal indicators and power quality features is further analyzed. Finally, the proposed data acquisition lightweight method is validated using both real-field measured data and PSCAD simulation. Results show that the proposed non-sinusoidal power system can effectively reflect the state of fundamental and harmonic voltage and current, represent multi-dimensional characteristics of the system, and achieve lightweight data acquisition utilizing<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> limited data.

articleTitle: A Harmonic Phase Reshaping Control Strategy for Minimizing Secondary Harmonic Injection in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The secondary harmonic sources in DC microgrids exhibit dispersity and unpredictability, posing significant challenges to the capacity design of filters. Existing filtering methods overlook neglect the potential for harmonic cancellation, leading to an excessive reliance on large-capacity filters. This paper proposed a harmonic phase reshaping strategy that maximizes harmonic cancellation by adjusting the harmonic phase, thus minimizing the harmonics injected into DC microgrids. Firstly, a optimal harmonic phase generator is developed that iteratively generates reference phases by following the negative gradient direction of the total harmonic amplitude. Subsequently, a harmonic phase tracker is introduced, which adjusts the voltage phase to align the harmonic phase with the reference phase. This method can reduce the total harmonics to zero or below the level of the largest single harmonic, thereby significantly decreasing the configuration capacity of the filter. Simulation results in RTLAB show that the proposed method can achieve optimal harmonic cancellation, effectively reducing the filtering burden in DC microgrids.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power System Protective Relays Based on Multi-Agent System Combined with Conservative Power Theory for Highly penetrated Renewable Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Inverter based resources (IBR) such as energy storage and renewable energy generators (REGs) are increasingly integrated into the grid. Typically, the fault current of IBRs are limited to 1.2 to 1.5 per unit. An over current relay designed for a synchronous generator will malfunction if the SG is replaced with an IBR. Thus, it is desirable to have an adaptive protection strategies to deal with various operating conditions due to different penetration level of REGs, topology configuration, and operation modes (grid-connected or islanded). Multiagent system (MAS) has been shown to have unique advantages for power system protection because agents operate autonomously and make decisions based on local information, which improves the speed and accuracy of fault detection. In this paper, we proposed to use MAS in combination with conservative power theory (CPT) for protection scheme to deal with IBR-dominated grid. Since CPT allows current to be decomposed into active, reactive, and void currents, it has better adaptedness in dealing with IBRs. We will show how to design an overcurrent relays and differential relays by means of MAS combined with CPT. The presented cases are some preliminary studies on how advanced power theory can be used to solve protection problems in the modern grid.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of a Photovoltaic Grid-Connected Harmonic Filter Based on Adaptive Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Addressing the slow response issues of current technologies in managing dynamic harmonic environments in distributed photovoltaic grid-connected systems, this paper proposes a harmonic filter model based on adaptive neural networks. This filter is designed on an improved Long Short-Term Memory network model, capable of real-time harmonic identification and filtering through self-learning and adaptive adjustment, thus enhancing the filter's performance and stability. Simulation experiments conducted on the Simulink platform revealed three key findings: first, the total harmonic distortion of harmonic current can be significantly reduced from an initial high value to below 3%; second, the response time is within 10 ms, significantly outperforming traditional filters; third, the filtering efficiency remains above 90%, indicating substantial advantages in harmonic management. Its high-efficiency filtering effect, rapid dynamic response capability, and intelligent adaptive capabilities demonstrate high potential in improving photovoltaic grid-connected harmonic management.

articleTitle: Analysis and Suppression of Circulating Current in Multiparalleled APFs with Grid Current Detected
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Typically, to cope with the harmonic pollution, active power filters (APFs) are installed in power system. And they will be connected in parallel when meeting higher compensation demand in industrial applications. However, the circulating current emerges in the multiparalleled APFs with grid current detected. It will induce the DC voltage oscillation of multiparalleled APFs and eventually lead to the system shutdown. Therefore, in this article, the underlying mechanism of circulating current is analyzed, and its main frequency region is determined. It is demonstrated that the circulating current originates from the grid current feedback control and undamped circulating current path among multiparalleled APFs. To suppress the circulating current, this article proposes a virtual resistor method incorporated in the basic control, which emulates a resistor connected with the filter inductor in series. In this way, the circulating current path can be damped, which further eliminates the circulating current. Finally, simulations are conducted to verify the correctness of mechanism analysis and effectiveness of proposed virtual resistor method.

articleTitle: An Enhanced TPA-LSTM Method for PMU Data Recovery and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The integrity of power system data is crucial for the operation and control of the grid. However,due to the integration of a large number of new energy sources and power electronic devices, phasor measurement units (PMU) suffer from all kinds of data losses. Therefore, this paper proposes a method that combines Enhanced Temporal Pattern Attention mechanism with Long Short-Term Memory (ETPA-LSTM). This method transforms the temporal pattern matrix of TPA to effectively extract features of different dimensions. It achieves high-precision prediction and recovery using only single-channel data from PMU. Case studies demonstrate that this method exhibits outstanding recovery accuracy under single-point and multi-point losses, as well as in scenarios of normal system operation and low-frequency oscillations. This method addresses the issue of data loss in complex systems and lays a solid foundation for the better application of PMU in power system.

articleTitle: Current Electric Load Forecasting Based on WOA-VMD-LSSVM
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In order to improvement of the accuracy of the short-term performance system load prediction and ensure a normal operation of daily power system, forecasting short term load model on the basis of WOA-VMD-LSSVM was proposed. To begin with, The Whale Optimisation Algorithm (WOA) is used to automatically select the best search for a optimal core parameters (K-value and penalty factor α) of the the variational modal decomposition (VMD) to get the best decomposition subsequence, reduce the following applies trend information to the prediction precision, and decompose a data by using the optimized VMD; after that, the decomposed data sets are inputted into the model separately, and each subsequence's predictions are summed to produce the final prediction. After that, decomposed groups about information is input in the pattern separately, and the forecasting scores of each of the sub-sequence summed to get the latest results of the forecast. To a certain extent, it provides a scientific decision-making basis for load management and optimal power dispatching.

articleTitle: A Harmonic Level Estimation Method Driven by Accessible Basic Electricity Data
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper presents a harmonic level estimation methodology for distribution networks based on accessible basic electricity data (A-BED), such as current, voltage, and power. The method employs a long and short-term memory network (LSTM) to assess the harmonic level. Firstly, a chronological law of harmonic emission level is extracted from electricity consumption information data through LSTM, with the aim of fitting the nonlinear relationship between current, voltage and power data and harmonic level. Secondly, the harmonic level of the current system is estimated through real-time A-BED, with the objective of achieving the visualization of harmonic level independently of harmonic monitoring equipment. The case studies illustrate that the proposed method is an efficacious approach for estimating the harmonic level of the current system, based on real-time A-BED from the power grid. The method exhibits high accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Research on Inrush Current Suppression of No-load Transformer Closing Based on Circuit Breaker Action Time Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The inrush current produced by the no-load transformer closing is prone to cause problems such as differential protection device malfunction. Currently, circuit breaker controlled closing devices are used to suppress excitation inrush current. The key to achieving controlled closing of circuit breakers is to make them close at the optimal moment. This research suggests a no-load transformer shutting inrush current suppression technique based on circuit breaker action time prediction to address this problem. This approach builds a BP neural network model training set by taking into account variables such as control voltage and ambient temperature. Then optimizes the circuit breaker action time prediction results using the Grey Wolf Optimizer algorithm. Simulation of excitation inrush of no-load transformer under different closing modes is carried out. The proposed controlled closing method, based on the prediction of circuit breaker action time, is shown to be effective in reducing the peak excitation inrush current to 0.45 times the rated current. This method can achieve greater closing inrush suppression.

articleTitle: Voltage Sag Assessment Method Based on Dynamic Identification of Distribution Network Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In contexts where renewable energy significantly integrates into distribution networks, the network topology frequently changes, rendering traditional fixed-topology methods for voltage sag assessment inadequate. This paper introduces a novel method that leverages voltage monitoring data to identify tie switch statuses and dynamically updates the node admittance matrix for assessing voltage sags. The effectiveness and accuracy of this approach are validated through MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Design of a New SSTS Topology for Switching Peak Voltage Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Solid state transfer switch (SSTS) is the core equipment for automatic switching of different power supplies. The existing SSTS based on LC resonance artificial construction of zero crossing has the problems of requiring capacitor pre-charging DC power supply, switching spike voltage and complex control. Therefore, this paper proposes a new SSTS topology to suppress the switching peak voltage. The AC power supply charges resonant capacitor through an uncontrollable rectifier circuit. The reflow diode is used to recover the excess energy of capacitor, and the problem of load peak voltage and current is eliminated. In addition, the resonant equivalent inductance is reduced under the action of the reflow diode, which can improve the switching speed. This work provides technical support for ensuring the uninterrupted power supply of sensitive loads, improving the operation performance of equipment and the treatment effect.

articleTitle: Dynamic Voltage Restorer Based on RTH Optimized PID and MPR Composite Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) controls the inverter through a double PID control system of inductor current and load voltage, but its compensation effect and stability are poor when the voltage contains more harmonics. A compound control strategy based on Red-tailed hawk algorithm (RTH) optimized PID and Modified Proportional Resonant (MPR) double closed-loop controller is proposed. In view of the problems existing in the present control method, MPR control is proposed for the voltage loop, which can realize no static error compensation for the load voltage under harmonic injection. The optimized PID control is adopted for the current loop, which can ensure that the DVR device can effectively and stably compensate the load voltage sag. Ultimately, the proposed composite control strategy's efficacy and superiority are substantiated through theoretical scrutiny and simulations.

articleTitle: The Risk Assessment Method of Large Power Grid Voltage Sag Considering the User Side
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The existing grid voltage sag assessment has considered the factors affecting the voltage sag on the grid side, and has not modeled the user tolerance characteristics and the voltage sag governance. Therefore, it is difficult to accurately reflect the level of voltage sag risk. Aiming at the above problems, we proposes a method to evaluate the voltage sag risk of large-scale power grids, which takes into account the user's tolerance characteristics and governance level. Firstly, considering that the detailed modeling is difficult to be applied, the method of establishing the external characteristic model of user tolerance and governance equipment is proposed. Secondly, the above two types of external characteristic models are implemented in the grid model of PSD-BPA, and the effect of the external equivalent users and the governance scheme is simulated. Thirdly, a comprehensive voltage sag evaluation index based on entropy weight method is proposed, and the voltage sag value and load loss of each node in the whole network are obtained by parallel simulation, and the risk of voltage sag is evaluated. Finally, the IEEE118 node system is used for simulation analysis, and the accuracy and practicability of the method are verified.

articleTitle: MMC Circulating Current Suppression Strategy based on PCHD-SMC Control
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In view of the two-octave circulation problem in the operation of modular multilevel converter (MMC), the traditional control method can no longer meet the stability and dynamic response of the system. Combined with the nonlinearity and passivity of MMC, this paper proposes a passive sliding mode (Port-Controlled Hamiltonian with Dissipation-Sliding-Mode Control) (PCHD-SMC) control strategy under three working conditions: steady-state operation, active power abrupt change and grid-side voltage abrupt change. Firstly, the Euler-Lagrange (EL) model of the modular multilevel converter was constructed, and the generation mechanism of the internal circulation was analyzed. Secondly, the passivity of MMC is analyzed, and the passive controller based on the EL model is applied to the current inner loop control. Then, sliding mode control is introduced to solve the problem that passive control is too dependent on parameters, which increases the robustness of the system and realizes the suppression of the two-fold circulation component. Finally, a 23-level MMC inverter simulation model was built in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Harmonic Modeling of a Six-Pulse Rectifier Under Various Power Supply Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the development of power systems towards power electronics, the integration capacity of renewable energy into the grid has been significantly enhanced. The power system is progressing towards modernization, intelligence, and sustainability. However, the integration of large-scale power electronic loads has also led to certain power quality issues in the grid, affecting the stable operation of the power network. Addressing the harmonic issues in power quality, this paper investigates the harmonic source model of a thyristor-based six-pulse rectifier and constructs its frequency domain harmonic model under different power supply conditions. First, the characteristic harmonic coupling admittance matrix model of the rectifier load under ideal power supply conditions is studied and established. On this basis, the non-characteristic harmonic coupling admittance matrix model of the rectifier load under unbalanced power supply conditions is developed. The unbalanced component detection method based on the Second-Order Generalized Integrator (SOGI) is utilized to detect and assess the three-phase balance. Ultimately, a harmonic model of the six-pulse rectifier adaptable to various power supply conditions is constructed. The accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed model are validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: A Non-Synchronous Harmonic State Estimation Strategy Based on Redundant Virtual Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Existing harmonic state estimation methods are mostly based on synchronized measurement data. However, due to various technical and economic constraints, the coverage of synchronized measurement devices in power grids is relatively low. In contrast, the penetration rate of power quality online monitoring systems (PQMS) is much higher, but the monitoring data from different nodes are not synchronized. To address this issue, a non-synchronous harmonic state estimation strategy based on redundant virtual measurements is proposed. The method introduces compensated phases to the non-synchronous monitoring data and constructs a synchronized nonlinear harmonic state estimation model. A non-synchronous phase compensation method based on redundant virtual measurements is also proposed to improve the observability of the harmonic state across the entire grid.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation for Power Quality Disturbance Data
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: During the acquisition of power quality disturbance data, the data quality may be affected to varying degrees due to system equipment failures or human maloperations. Accurate evaluation of the data availability level is a prerequisite for subsequent data cleaning and analysis. The existing methods usually adopt a single index to evaluate the partial data quality but are difficult to quantify to what extent the data can be utilized in the following analysis. In view of this, combined with its own characteristics of the power quality disturbance, this paper adopts multiple monitoring frequency correlation to evaluate the data timeliness. For the accuracy evaluation fails to detect the connection errors, an accuracy evaluation method based on the hierarchical rule test is proposed to improve the reliability After analyzing the influence of different dimension data qualities on the perturbation analysis results, the availability evaluation method of the power quality disturbance data is proposed.

articleTitle: Modelling and Experimental Validation of Interharmonic Emission of an Inverter-Driven Heat-pump
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Interharmonic modelling and experimental verification of an inverter-driven heat-pump (HP) under different power levels is considered in this paper. Results of a research activity, conducted first in New Zealand at the University of Canterbury (UC) and then in Italy at the University of Campania (UCLV), are reported. The aim is to examine the effect of interharmonics on the low voltage network produced by HPs. The time-domain model developed in another paper from some of the authors for harmonic studies and experimentally validated by measurements made in the field is here extended to model also interharmonics. Very accurate results in terms of interharmonic injection are obtained, which will allow the use of the proposed model in more comprehensive harmonic and interharmonic penetration studies in the time and frequency domains.

articleTitle: Research on Negative Harmonics Suppression Results of Parallel Active Filter in the State of Under-compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Parallel active filters may exhibit negative harmonics suppression results in the state of under-compensation, which will cause harmonics amplification in the surrounding power grid. In this paper, the reason for negative harmonics suppression is analyzed based on the principle of active filtering technology. The electrical scenarios that are prone to negative harmonics suppression are summarized and classified. The concept of harmonic short-circuit ratio is proposed. When the harmonic short-circuit ratio falls on a specific position in the complex plane, there may be negative harmonics suppression, presented as harmonic voltage amplification, harmonic current amplification, or both amplification. Finally the rationality of the theoretical analysis is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Performance of Ideal and Practical Concentric Magnetic Gears in High Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Ideally, magnetic gears (MGs) have numerous advantages relative to their classical mechanical counterparts. In practice, however, MGs face numerous electromagnetic and mechanical challenges that must be considered in high speed applications. This paper describes a comparative study between an ideal and a practical concentric magnetic gear of the same size in terms of torque capability, magnetic flux density in the air gaps and power loss in the iron and magnets. Both topologies were evaluated by means of 2-dimentional finite element analysis using COMSOL Multiphysics® as a simulation tool. The main findings are that practical high-speed MGs require larger air gaps, weaker magnets and mechanical reinforcements, which lead to significantly lower power transmission capability.

articleTitle: Harmonic Suppression Strategy Based on High-voltage Active Resonance Suppressor for Offshore Wind Farms using AC Transmission Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Aiming at the serious problem of background harmonic amplification in Offshore Wind Farm with Long-distance AC Submarine Cable (OWF-LACSC) integrated system, impedance model of a domestic OWFs-LACSC system is established firstly. In consideration of the positive and negative sequence properties of sub-background harmonics in the power grid, a single channel is designed to mitigate two odd background harmonics with opposing positive and negative sequence characteristics by leveraging the fundamental frequency shift feature of Parker transform. Combining with resistive active power filter technology, a high-voltage active resonance suppressor and its control strategy are proposed, and the parameter feasible domain of the channel under different frequency harmonic suppression targets is established to carry out parameter optimization design. Finally, the electromagnetic transient model of an OWFs-LACSC system is built in PSCAD to verify the feasibility and robustness of the proposed device and control strategy.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation Strategy for Inverter Considering Data Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the integration of inverter-based distributed generation in the distribution network, it is important to utilize inverters for voltage regulation to improve voltage quality. However, it is highly dependent on the communication system and in practice it is difficult to avoid data quality issues. A voltage regulation strategy for the inverter considering data quality is proposed to ensure the effectiveness of regulation. Firstly, an estimation method of acquired data is proposed based on distribution station area (DSA) similarity to filter similar DSA clusters by cosine similarity algorithm, and estimate the acquired data to centrally coordinate multiple inverters. Secondly, a voltage regulation decision-making set construction method is proposed based on association data mining, which can achieve the evaluation of voltage regulation instructions. Finally, a voltage regulation strategy for the inverter considering data quality is proposed for the distribution network control center and DSA. The simulation results have verified the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed strategy, which can effectively support the operation of the inverter and guarantee the voltage quality of distribution network in the event of data quality issues.

articleTitle: Treatment Method of Intercurrent Power Quality Problems in Low-Voltage AC/DC Hybrid Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: As the "carbon peaking and carbon neutrality" strategy and new power systems are progressively advanced, a significant portion of new energy sources and loads are integrated into low-voltage distribution networks. This integration makes it increasingly challenging to address concurrent power quality issues in real-time. Deep reinforcement learning, which benefits from "offline training and online deployment," presents a viable solution for managing real-time power quality issues in ADHDN (AC/DC hybrid distribution networks). This paper first establishes an MDP (Markov Decision Process) environment grounded in the Disflow calculation method. Subsequently, the "Deep Q-learning" reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to train an agent, enabling real-time management of concurrent power quality issues in low-voltage ADHDN. Finally, a case study involving a 21-node low-voltage ADHDN demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in handling real-time concurrent power quality issues.

articleTitle: Voltage Sag Risk Assessment Based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the ongoing advancement of high and emerging technologies, precision power electronic equipment that is highly sensitive to voltage sags has become increasingly prevalent in industrial production. Due to the randomness and severity of voltage sag events, a large number of industrial economic losses and user complaints have been caused. Voltage sag assessment integrates information from both the grid side and the sensitive equipment on the user side to evaluate the risk of voltage sag at specific nodes. This approach allows power supply companies and users to better understand the potential risks associated with voltage sags. It also serves as a theoretical foundation for users to choose optimal connection points based on their specific conditions and to address voltage sag issues effectively. This paper analyzes the main reasons why users are affected by voltage sag, uses the deep neural network model to explore the potential relationship between the actual influencing factors and the user's voltage sag risk, and uses the comprehensive voltage sag index to evaluate the user's voltage sag risk. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified through real calculation examples.

articleTitle: Harmonic Suppression Model Based on Economic Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: There are significant harmonics in distribution network, which can affect the operation of power equipment, increase losses, interfere with communications, reduce product quality, and even cause safety accidents, and effective suppression of which is of great significance to ensure system stability. In this paper, a model for harmonic suppression based on economic optimization is proposed to optimize the harmonic suppression cost to the minimum while satisfying constraints such as all nodes in distribution network have lower than standard total harmonic voltage distortion. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model can realize all nodes harmonics not exceeding the standard in different cases and can greatly reduce the cost of harmonic suppression compared to APF. This proves that the model can well solve the technical and economic problems of harmonic suppression, and lays the foundation for practical application.

articleTitle: Quantification of Electricity Power Balance Based on Optimisation of Time-series Combinations of Multiple Types of Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: As renewable energy generation expands, the challenge of power equilibrium in the evolving power system intensifies. Integrating flexible loads into the regional grid's power balance management contributes to resolving issues related to renewable energy consumption and curtailment of wind and solar output. This study intricately models thermal power stations, diverse hydroelectric facilities, and flexible loads, establishing an optimization model that encompasses multiple resource types with the aim of minimizing the overall system operating cost. Through case study analysis, the effectiveness and financial viability of the proposed approach are demonstrated. Findings indicate that involving flexible loads in regional grid power balance significantly improves the region's capacity to absorb renewable energy and concurrently enhances economic efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation for Photovoltaic-Energy Storage System-Integrated Distribution Network Based on Adaptive Expectation Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive expectation-based improved genetic algorithm (AE-IGA) for the photovoltaic (PV)-energy storage system (ESS)-integrated distribution network, which helps to improve power quality (PQ) and renewable energy sources consumption. Three optimization objectives are considered in the PV-ESS-integrated distribution network, including maximizing economic benefits, minimizing voltage deviation, and maximizing the power factor. To avoid the complicated decision mechanism, obvious subjectivity and poor applicability in the multi-objective optimization problem (MOPs), the IGA is firstly utilized to obtain the Pareto set (PS) of MOPs. Then, an AE method is designed for selecting the desired nondominated solution from the PS. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves the PV penetration and reduces voltage deviation, and improves the power factor in the distribution network.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning-Based Solutions for Fault Classification and Region Identification in Onshore Wind Farm Collector Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the increasing expansion of renewable energy resources, wind farms are becoming predominant, especially with the progress of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs). Although IBRs are operationally effective, it is recognized that this generation type has directly impacted the operation of protection and fault diagnosis functions. In this context, this paper investigates the potential of Machine Learning (ML)-based solutions for classifying faults and identifying faulted regions in onshore wind farm collector systems. For the studies, a realistic wind farm system topology is modeled in PSCAD software, and fault scenarios are represented in the collector systems with different fault parameters and wind farm generation levels. These studies highlight the best-performing ML methods for fault diagnosis within onshore wind farms and provide insights on the best measurement points for successful fault classification and fault region identification.

articleTitle: Federated Learning with LSTM Neural Network for Regional Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed energy resources at the grid edge, including renewable energy generation, flexible loads, and energy storage devices, accurately predicting consumer-level distributed generation and consumption has become crucial. However, conventional centralized processing and machine learning approaches are impractical because of data security and privacy issues. This paper proposes a load forecasting method based on federated learning with LSTM neural network which updates model parameters by having clients responsible for model training and a server responsible for model aggregation, allowing multiple clients to collaboratively train a machine learning model without sharing raw data. Simulation results show that this method can achieve accurate predictions while preserving privacy.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Comprehensive Compensation Strategy for Multi-Voltage Level Traction Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Power quality (PQ) problem and insufficient supply capacity have been challenges for long-distance traction power supply system (LD-TPSS). LD-TPSS based on high-voltage traction cables can enhance the power supply capacity. However, it triggers the end supply voltage overrun easily. In this paper, a new multi-voltage (MV-) TPSS is proposed, it can ensure the power supply capacity, regulate the voltage and realize the PQ management. Then, a comprehensive compensation strategy with a hierarchical structure is proposed. In the upper layer, voltage and PQ are managed in two stages to calculate the compensation power demand. The first stage, system voltage reactive power flow optimization is optimized. The second stage, unified management of PQ such as VU and power factor (PF) is completed. The control of each compensation device is realized by the lower controller. Finally, a detailed case comparison demonstrates the correctness and effectiveness of the system topology and strategy.

articleTitle: The Improvement of Small Interference Synchronous Stability of Photovoltaic Grid-connected Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) can be effectively implemented to improve the stability of new energy grid-connected inverters. Power oscillation can be effectively suppressed by adjusting the moment of inertia and damping of VSG according to the operating state. In this paper, a phase compensation strategy for PLL is proposed to reduce its negative damping to enhance the stability of small disturbances. First of all, the grid-connected inverter model controlled by virtual synchronous generator is established, and the damping torque model including the converter and the complete control dynamics of the grid is derived. Then the SISO stability criterion of grid-connected system is obtained based on damping torque model. The influence of damping coefficient on the stability of single-stage three-phase PV grid-connected converter system is analyzed. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed method can improve the stability of small disturbance.

articleTitle: A New Three+Phase Unbalanced Optimal Control Strategy of Distribution Network Based on Function Reuse of Micro-Source Grid-Connected Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Considering the quality of the output voltage, the distributed power supply needs to have a certain power quality control ability when the unbalanced fault occurs. In response to this requirement, this paper proposes a parallel system. An inverter is placed at the common coupling point of the main circuit and the power grid as an external device for fault ride-through when a serious fault drop. During normal operation, the parallel inverter does not operate, and the main circuit inverter outputs active power. Under asymmetric fault conditions, the parallel inverter injects reactive power to the common coupling point to limit AC current and grid voltage support. Firstly, the power model of the inverter under asymmetric conditions is analyzed in the first part. Then, the power quality management and capacity optimization strategy of the parallel system are described. Finally, the waveform results show the correctness and superiority of the capacity optimization strategy.

articleTitle: Common Errors in FFT Analysis due to Inadequate Period Usage: Introducing the VFID Method as Solution Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Accurate modeling of variable frequency distributed generation (DG) systems is essential for understanding their behavior and optimizing performance. Conventional methods often struggle to capture individual ripple information, hindering accurate representation of variable frequency systems. This paper introduces the variable frequency interharmonic domain (VFID) method as a solution to common errors encountered with traditional methods, such as spectral leakage and aliasing introduced by the fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm. VFID offers precise ripple information without the need for additional post-processing routines, ensuring robust analysis of variable frequency DG systems. By mitigating errors associated with FFT analysis, VFID enhances the accuracy and reliability of frequency domain representations, leading to improved system design and operation in power quality analysis applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sub-synchronous Oscillation Suppression Strategy for Doubly Fed Wind Farm Connected to Series Compensated System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: To suppress the sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) with a wide range of time-varying frequency characteristic of doubly fed wind farm connected to series compensated (DWF + SC) system, this paper proposes a modified adaptive linear element (ADALINE) SSO suppression (MA-SOS) strategy for Doubly fed Induction Generators. Compared to the classical SSO suppression strategies, the MA-SOS controller consists of an ADALINE filter-based SSO suppression (A-SOS) module, a frequency identification module to obtain real-time dominant SSO frequency as well as a frequency locking module to update the reference frequency of A-SOS, achieving the high adaptability of SSO suppression under various operating conditions. With the advantages of simple control structure, easy control implementation and superior filtering effect, MA-SOS is also independent of accurate mathematical model of the system. Finally, simulation verification and comparisons are carried out, showing that MA-SOS can effectively suppress SSO in different frequencies with satisfactory robustness and superior performance over existing classical SSO suppressing strategies.

articleTitle: Transient Disturbance Modeling of 10kV Power Distribution Cable Mutual Impedance
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Accurate mutual impedance parameters are crucial for capturing transient disturbance signals using cable induction effects. This study measured the cable mutual impedance spectra within the transient disturbance frequency range of 0.1-20 kHz through real 10 kV power distribution cable experiments. Based on experimental data, a mutual impedance equivalent frequency-dependent model was obtained using vector fitting algorithm and circuit synthesis theory. Through transient induction voltage experiments, the modeling results were compared with commonly used transient simulation software PSCAD's built-in cable model and the steady-state inductance model. It was shown that the transient disturbance induction voltage calculated by the model in this paper can more accurately reflect its pulse and fluctuation details, making it more suitable for precise analysis of transient disturbances. This work confirms the necessity of specifically modeling cable mutual impedance for transient disturbance analysis, providing accurate parameter basis and new focal points for transient disturbance analysis.

articleTitle: An Improved Inertia Measurement Method Based on EMD Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the introduction of dual-carbon goals, large-scale renewable energy units have been connected to the power system via power electronic devices, which leads to a reduction and uneven distribution of system inertia. According to reference [1] and reference [2], the conventional concept of average inertia fails to accurately reflect the inertia levels within specific regions. Therefore, online inertia measurements at different locations of the system becomes important. Due to the interaction of synchronous machines in the power system, low-frequency oscillations pose challenges to the accuracy of inertia measurements. To tackle this issue, this paper uses the empirical mode decomposition (EMD) method to eliminate the side effect of the low-frequency oscillation components in the frequency response curve and employs the second-order rotor swing equation of the generator to achieve precise measurement of inertia. Finally, the IEEE three-machine nine-node model is used to verify the correctness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Passitivity Enhancement Strategy for Voltage Controlled Aviation Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the rapid development of more electric aircraft technology, the aircraft power supply system contains more constant power loads. For the purpose of improving the power supply system stability, this paper proposes a second order generalized integrator (SOGI) based current feed-forward active damping strategy to realize system passivity from 0Hz up to the Nyquist frequency, and thus mitigate the harmonic oscillations caused by the nonlinear and inductive loads. A 5kW three-phase mid-frequency inverter based on LC filter is built in the laboratory. The experimental results show that the proposed control strategy and parameter tuning method can effectively enhance the system passivity and improves the compatibility of the inverter and the load.

articleTitle: Vectorization Analysis of Voltage Sag Considering on Energy Index
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: By analyzing the causes and characteristics of various voltage sags, the shortcomings of current description of voltage sags are introduced, and a voltage sags vector considering energy index is proposed. At the equipment level, based on the in-depth analysis of equipment voltage tolerance capacity, an equipment voltage sag severity vector considering energy index is proposed. At the process level, by analyzing the relationship between semiconductor equipment and industrial process, a process voltage sag severity vector based on SEMI F47 curve and considering the sag energy index is proposed. Based on the analysis of process immune time, the concept of process parameter immune time (PIT) is proposed, and process strain vector based on PIT is proposed. The proposed process strain vector can introduce the vector correlation operation into the analysis of industrial process sag consequence state, which has very important practical significance and theoretical value.

articleTitle: Optimization of an Asymmetrical 5-level Cascaded H-Bridge Inverter Modulation by Evaluation of Dead Times Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Artificial intelligence, born after neural networks, finds application in different fields of science. The algorithms for evaluating the best solutions can be applied in different aspects of power quality. Specifically, the paper presents the possibility of using asymmetric voltages, due for example to strings of different photovoltaic panels, and emulating the behavior of a 7-level staircase with a 5 level CHBMLI. The optimization algorithm exploits the command of the insertion of the inverter legs to eliminate or mythologize the harmonics that can be injected into the network. Attention is placed on dead times, essential to avoid short circuits and makes use of the black widow technique.

articleTitle: Harmonic Measurement and Analysis in Manufacturing Industry: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Power Quality (PQ) has gained significant importance in recent years and is one of the critical aspects of modern manufacturing plants. Harmonics is one of the important Power Quality disturbances and many failures of critical components in industry are observed due to it. This paper presents the case study of harmonic measurement in a manufacturing industry which was facing the issues of stoppage of critical processes due to harmonics. Extensive PQ measurements using Class A & Class S power quality loggers were performed in March and May 2024 in the industrial plant located in Chakan, Pune (India). It was observed that the HVAC load was causing harmonics distortion of 29.1% with dominant 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order harmonics and was injecting 46 A harmonic current. Shifting of the HVAC feeder load on the raw power resulted in an 81% reduction in the total harmonic current and a reduction of voltage THD from 2% to 0.66%. Detailed analysis of PQ measurements of UPS Output with and without HVAC load with the help of waveforms and harmonic spectrums is presented. Active harmonic filter sizing to improve the power quality of the industry is presented.

articleTitle: Analytical Analysis on DC Capacitance Voltage Dip Amplitude of AC Adjustable-Speed Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the development of society, the frequency of Adjustable-Speed Drives (ASD) usage among industrial users has surged. ASDs are highly sensitive to voltage dips, when the DC capacitance voltage drops below a certain threshold, the ASD low voltage protection is triggered. However, this threshold is set based on voltage tolerance curve (VTC) and is subjective, quantitative analysis on the amplitude of DC capacitor voltage dips in ASDs is lacking. Therefore, this paper constructs a dynamic model of the ASD grid-connected system on a transient time scale and obtains an approximate analytical solution for the power absorbed by the ASD from the grid. Furthermore, by establishing a dynamic model of the capacitor voltage during speed regulation and grid voltage dips caused by the single line-to-ground fault, and based on the Fourier expansion method, the approximate analytical solution for the amplitude of ASD capacitor voltage dips is obtained. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is validated by simulation and calculation.

articleTitle: Abnormal State Estimation of Shunt Capacitor Banks Based on Transient Power Disturbance Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Shunt capacitor banks are essential for reactive power compensation to ensure voltage stability and reduce system losses. Capacitor banks consist of multiple units with components in series and parallel. A small number of component failures will not immediately affect the safe operation of the capacitor bank. However, due to component breakdown, the capacitance voltage will be redistributed, which will have an impact on other devices. Practical operational experience shows that capacitors generate many transient disturbance signals when some components exhibit breakdown. Quantitative analysis of the transient disturbance signals can find capacitor anomalies, allowing the extraction of transient disturbance characteristics based on the Prony algorithm. The transient signals quantitatively estimate the phase and number of capacitors that break down to judge capacitor anomalies. In this paper, PSCAD/EMTDC provide a verification model. Thus, the theoretical analyses and correctness of the detection algorithm are verified.

articleTitle: PMU Measurement Accuracy Awareness Provided by Power Quality Indices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Phasor measurement units (PMUs) are measurement devices capable of monitoring voltage and current phasors, frequency and rate of change of frequency considering an absolute time reference for phase angle evaluation. The absolute reference is provided by coordinated universal time (UTC) through global navigation satellite system signals and distributed to PMUs through appropriate protocols or dedicated receivers. The quality level of time synchronization is directly related to the quality of the measurement as it affects the phase-angle evaluation. This relationship is taken into account and communicated through dedicated fields in the data packets containing the PMU measurements. However, other factors can affect the quality of the measurements, such as changes in the signal or the presence of disturbances. These influencing factors, or, in general, the operating conditions in which the PMUs are immersed while providing measurements, are typically not evaluated in real-time. For this purpose, a real-time estimation of the PMU measurement conditions is presented in this paper. Such estimation is carried out on the basis of the information provided by power quality indices. The goal is to accompany measured quantities with information on the measurement quality that can be helpful for proper use of the collected measurements.

articleTitle: Arc Fault Detection of Electric Bicycle Based on FTS- DPC
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Arc fault is one of the important causes of electric bicycle fires. However, the current research on arc fault detection for electric bicycles is not mature enough. In this paper, we propose an arc fault detection method based on multi-domain arc features and improved Density Peak Clustering. Firstly, the current signal of arc fault in the charging state of electric bicycle is collected, and the Tamura texture feature is extracted after the signal is two-dimensional imaged by Markov Transition Field method. In order to avoid the instability of a single feature, time domain and frequency domain features are extracted as supplements. Secondly, due to the randomness of arc, the feature value of arc samples fluctuates greatly and overlaps with the normal samples, which will decrease the detection accuracy. Therefore, an improved Density Peak Clustering method based on Fuzzy Threshold Screening is proposed.
