The optimal fuzzy threshold is obtained by training, according to the threshold screening results, the feature values of normal samples and arc samples are mapped to 0 and 1 respectively, which increases the inter-class difference and reduces the intra-class difference. Finally, the arc fault detection is realized based on the Density Peak Clustering method. The test accuracy in the experimental results is 99.4%, which is higher than other arc fault detection methods.

articleTitle: Automatic Power Quality Disturbance Feature Extraction Using Fast Iterative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Power quality (PQ) events have become increasingly complex due to the growing integration of renewable energy resources into electric grids. Hence, there is a pressing need for expressive latent representations of the sensorized grid components that can aid the timely detection of PQ disturbances (PQDs). Nevertheless, traditional feature extraction methods, including those based on frequency or decomposed time domains, are generally appropriate for specific subsets of possible PQDs and heavily rely on theoretical or experiential intuition. To address these challenges, this study introduces fast iterative filtering (FIF)—an entirely data-driven approach for uncovering hidden features within disturbed signals. FIF utilizes iterative convolution with a filter constructed from the signal itself to decompose non-stationary signals into intrinsic mode functions, eliminating the need for prior knowledge. Furthermore, fast Fourier transform (FFT) is embedded to improve computational efficiency, enabling real-time recognition of PQDs. Evaluated using synthetic signals per IEEE 1159-2019 standard, FIF shows excellent extraction performance, being capable of representing the predictive content of feature tensors, including interpretative patterns of PQDs.

articleTitle: Power Quality Governance Strategy of Active Distribution Network Based on Multi-phase Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In recent years, due to the large-scale integration of distributed energy sources in active distribution networks, severe over-voltage issues have emerged. A common solution is to install reactive power compensation devices, but the application scenarios of these devices are limited. With the widespread application of energy storage and electric vehicles in distribution networks, the active power output of energy storage systems and the V2G (Vehicle-to-Grid) interaction of electric vehicles not only address issues like peak shaving and valley filling, but also the reactive power and harmonic current output by their grid-connected inverters, when capacity permits, can be used to compensate the voltage quality of the distribution network. Therefore, this paper proposes a power quality management strategy for active distribution networks based on the collaborative optimization of energy storage systems and electric vehicles. This is achieved by establishing an Optimal Power Flow (OPF) model. Additionally, an Immune Comprehensive Learning Particle Swarm Optimization (ICLPSO) algorithm is used to optimize and determine the reactive power output of energy storage systems and electric vehicles. Finally, taking the voltage issues of the IEEE 162-node distribution network with distributed PV as an example, the effectiveness of the proposed management strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Voltage-Dependent EV Battery Charger Models for Power Flow and Harmonic Emission Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The ongoing large-scale electrification of road transportation sector will result in significantly increased demands from electric vehicle (EV) battery chargers (EVBCs), impacting not only network power flows and load profiles, but also power quality levels and harmonic emissions. Typically, on-board EVBCs are modelled as a "constant power" load type, without considering their voltage-dependent characteristics will result in errors in estimated component loading and harmonic emission limits, as well as required network upgrades to connect the new EV loads. This paper presents details of the development of two component-based EVBC models that incorporate both voltage dependency and state-of-charge dependency of their power demand and harmonic emission characteristics. The developed models are experimentally validated using actual measurement data under both sinusoidal and distorted input voltage supply conditions, demonstrating their applicability for assessing impact of EVBCs on network power flows and harmonic emission levels.

articleTitle: Dichotomous-Sliding Window Fourier Algorithm Based Broadband Oscillation Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The rapid development of modern power electronics technology has been accompanied by an increase in the number of nonlinear loads in the power system, which has led to a huge challenge for the safe operation of the power system. Traditional oscillation detection methods have problems such as large computation volume and poor real-time performance, which cannot meet the demand for oscillation detection and analysis in modern power systems. To this end, this paper proposes a dichotomous-sliding discrete Fourier transform (DSDFT) oscillation detection method, which can quickly and accurately detect the information of oscillation signals generated in power electronic systems. Firstly, the principle of the proposed oscillation detection method is introduced in this paper; then, the specific parameter design process of the detection method is analyzed and the signals of different oscillation forms are analyzed; finally, the simulation verification is carried out under the environment of MATLAB/SIMULINK, and the results show that the proposed oscillation detection method of this paper has small computation and short response time, and it can satisfy the demand of fast oscillation detection.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of CLCC-HVDC Based on Switching Function
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The new Controllable Line-Commuted Converter (CLCC) with controllable turn-off capability employs a hybrid design of thyristors, combining the low cost and high reliability of conventional converters. During AC faults or disturbances, it uses a flexible DC auxiliary circuit to achieve forced commutation, thereby addressing the commutation failure issues of LCC converters and enhancing the stability and reliability of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems. To study the characteristics of electric power quality and improvement measures in the AC/DC transmission system at the receiving end after integrating the new converter, a theoretical derivation based on modulation theory and commutation principles was conducted to explore the formation mechanisms of characteristic and non-characteristic harmonic components in the DC voltage and AC current. The harmonics of LCC-HVDC and CLCC-HVDC were analyzed in detail using FFT method on measured data from the converter stations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Harmonic State Estimation Algorithm for Distribution Networks Considering Pseudo Measurement of New Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The distribution network environment is complex and has serious harmonic problems. The large-scale integration of new energy has exacerbated the diversification of harmonic sources and voltage distortion. Aiming at the poor estimation accuracy of traditional dynamic harmonic state estimation algorithm when there are time-varying noise and abrupt data, an adaptive harmonic state estimation algorithm for distribution networks considering new energy pseudo-measurement is proposed. Firstly, the Sage-Husa noise estimation method based on the forgetting factor is introduced to estimate the time-varying noise interference when the noise covariance is reduced in real-time. Then, an adaptive factor is constructed to online correct the error variance matrix, thereby reducing the prediction error caused by sudden load changes. Secondly, a confidence interval pseudo measurement generation method for quantile regression Bayesian gated recurrent neural network is proposed to solve the problem of missing short-term harmonic data in new energy and improve effect of the real-time harmonic state estimation. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm proposed in this paper is verified by an modified distribution network system.

articleTitle: Automatic Identification of Harmonic Emission Patterns in Electricity Networks based on Clustering and Principal Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Power grids are undergoing significant changes, such as the increase in renewable energy sources and the large-scale introduction of electric vehicles. These changes have a substantial impact on Power Quality, particularly regarding harmonic distortion. Consequently, network operators conduct extensive measurement campaigns, resulting in vast amounts of data. This data contains highly valuable information about disturbance characteristics. One possibility to extract this information efficiently is the application of machine learning methods. This paper presents a method for identifying prevailing harmonic patterns in long-term measurements. By applying a clustering method combined with Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the proposed approach identifies prevailing harmonic patterns and highlights measurement sites that deviate from these patterns. Understanding these variations can help network operators gain better insights into their networks, optimize the number of PQ monitoring points, and identify sites with unique harmonic behavior. The proposed method is applied to long-term field measurements recorded at various sites within 110-kV networks supplying large cities in China.

articleTitle: Voltage Sag Stochastic Estimation Method Based on Two-Dimensional Trajectory of Multiple Monitoring Parameters for Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In distribution networks, the occurrence of voltage sag is widely recognized as one of the most disconcerting power quality phenomena. The assessment of the different levels of sag at diverse nodes is of considerable significance for the effective mitigation of voltage sag. Amidst the ongoing proliferation of distributed generators (DG), a discernible transformation in the fault attributes of distribution networks is taking place. Traditional voltage sag assessment methods based on stochastic fault simulation face several challenges: in accordance with prevailing grid standards, it is imperative for DG to possess ability against low voltage ride-through (LVRT) events, rendering them no longer equivalent to constant voltage sources during faults, making traditional assessment methods inadequate due to accuracy issues. Moreover, different units have varying LVRT strategy parameters that are difficult to obtain, making it challenging to establish accurate equivalent models of power sources. To address these challenges, this paper proposed a voltage sag stochastic estimation method based on the two-dimensional trajectory of multiple monitoring parameters for DG. Firstly, a two-dimensional trajectory was constructed based on various monitoring data, and a convolutional neural network model was utilized to automatically identify key control parameters such as reactive compensation coefficients during LVRT processes. Based on the parameter identification results, an equivalent model of DG under fault conditions was established. Subsequently, voltage sag stochastic estimation was achieved based on the Monte Carlo method. The proposed methodology's efficacy was substantiated by the outcomes of the simulation. The findings demonstrated that the proposed method accurately identified different unit control strategy parameters and achieved significantly improved accuracy in voltage sag stochastic estimation compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Applying Bayesian Optimization to Parameters Selection in Waveform Reconstruction of Time-Varying Components for Power Quality Study
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The widespread power electronics-based renewable energy resources and modern nonlinear loads in power systems present challenges in accurately assessing power quality due to their produced time-varying voltage and current waveforms. While several time-frequency analysis methods have been proposed to overcome the limitations of traditional frequency domain analysis, parameter adjustments are often needed for different types of signals. This paper focuses on applying Bayesian optimization to select the suitable parameters for the short-time Fourier-based multi-synchrosqueezing transform. The results obtained from simulations and actual measurements provide an appropriate range of parameter settings that reduce assessed time and validate the performance of the algorithm. Moreover, two feature importance indices emphasize the relevance and significance of the parameters.

articleTitle: Harmonic Challenges and Practical Solutions for Transmission Systems and Renewable Energy Zones
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Addressing harmonic challenges and proposing practical solutions for future transmission systems and Renewable Energy Zones is essential for Transmission Network Service Providers (TNSP), network operators, renewable energy stakeholders, and policymakers in Australia. Renewable Energy Zones are designed to facilitate the connection of large-scale renewable generation within localised areas, optimising the use of transmission infrastructure. While the integration of renewable generation offers significant benefits to network owners and consumers, it also introduces new harmonic challenges for network operators. Inverter-based renewable generation, such as solar and wind, can generate substantial harmonics in the power system. Simultaneously, the rapid retirement of coal-fired generators, which currently help absorb harmonics and provide damping effects within the network, exacerbates this issue. At present, TNSPs in Australia lack a standardised and robust approach to managing harmonics, leading to each TNSP developing its own bespoke harmonic management methodologies. This has resulted in inconsistent interpretations of the National Electricity Rules and associated standards, creating technical and financial challenges for network participants across various jurisdictions within the National Electricity Market. If these challenges are not addressed, they could hinder progress towards Australia's Renewable Energy Targets and delay the transition to Net Zero. This paper outlines the issues related to the current harmonic management practices employed by some TNSPs in Australia. It proposes practical steps and solutions to overcome the complex challenges of managing harmonics in transmission systems and Renewable Energy Zones.

articleTitle: A Review of Converters Embedded with Impedance Measurement of Li-ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) has been concerned increasingly due to its relationship with inner states of batteries, which has underlying possibility to be deployed in battery management systems (BMSs). However, the traditional impedance measurements of batteries are constrained in the laboratory condition. The urgent requirement is exploring a practicable and applicable measuring system of battery impedance having the following features: time-saving waveform of excitation, signal generating device with merits of low-cost, low energy consumption and space-saving, and high accuracy signal processing algorithm. For this demand, a lot of researches have been done from the views of signal with impedance extraction and excitation device, and the most promising application is converters embedded with EIS measurement. Literatures related were summarized and analyzed in hope that providing a new perspective and inspiration for developing a feasible measuring system.

articleTitle: Case Study of Load Shedding Caused by Voltage Sag: Mechanism Analysis and Optimization Measures
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Based on an actual fault case in the power grid, this article firstly summarizes and analyzes the network transmission of voltage sag event from high voltage level power grid to low voltage level power grid and the corresponding load reduction. Two categories for the causes for load reduction are summarized, i.e., sensitive equipment shutdown and distribution transformer tripping out. By comparing the operating data with the tolerance curves of computer equipment as well as semiconductor equipment, the reason for shutdown of sensitive equipment is revealed; by analyzing the protective action types of the distribution transformer, the reason for tripping out of distribution transformer is revealed. Then, the impact of under-voltage relay and tripping device is further analyzed. On the basis of the above analysis, the measures to reduce the impact of voltage sag and correspondingly load reduction are put forward from two aspects, i.e., protection configuration and parameter optimization setting, as well as cooperative management between power supply enterprises and important power users.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Voltage Regulation Techniques in PV Rich LV Feeders
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of the voltage regulation techniques currently used by electricity network service providers, specifically LV-STATCOM and Community Energy Storage, alongside modern inverter control functions, such as Volt-VAr and Volt-Watt responses. Modern inverters are equipped with built-in Volt-VAr and Volt-Watt functions for immediate use, while Rule-Based Control was selected for Energy Storage control, as it is commonly implemented in off-the-shelf residential storage devices. The aim of this paper is to enhance understanding of the efficacy of these voltage regulation techniques in terms of their voltage management performance and utilization of feeder capacity. To normalize network performance parameters, two indices are introduced: maximum voltage deviation and feeder reserve capacity, which analyze voltage management and the hosting capacity of the feeder, respectively. A case study 300 m, 4-wire, LV feeder based on typical Australian design parameters is used to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed control methods through a time-series power flow simulation in OpenDSS.

articleTitle: Multi-factor Sensitivity to Power Quality of Power Electronic Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the reduction of the price of photovoltaic (PV) panels and policy support, more and more PV power generation is being integrated into the grid. As PV inverters use power electronic devices, they will introduce harmonics into the grid, which can easily cause waveform distortion and equipment damage. At the same time, extensive access to PV can easily cause power back-feeding problems, resulting in over-voltage at the grid-connected point. It is very important to study the impact of PV parameter access on power quality at grid-connected points. However, the current research focuses on the impact of a single parameter, while in practical applications, the impact of PV access to power quality at the grid point of common coupling (PCC) varies due to different environments, installation locations, and so on. Therefore, this paper compares the effects of different irradiances, line impedance, and control parameters on total harmonic distortion (THD) and grid-connected point voltage under ideal and background harmonic scenarios through simulation experiments, and derives the parameter variation rules that are conducive to the reduction of THD and the control voltage in the stable domain. In the practical application, it can be used to guide the power quality improvement of grid-connected points.

articleTitle: Harmonic Performance Differences under Non-ideal Grid between Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Renewable energy generation devices need power electronic converters to be connected to the grid. Presently, the grid-following converter (GFL) and the grid-forming converter (GFM) are used in the electric power system for grid-connection control. As renewable energy progresses, power electronics play a growing role in power systems, leading to increased complexity in harmonic generation. The sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) and dead time can lead to the output of converter harmonics. Meanwhile, the grid voltage background harmonics also respond to the converter harmonics. Given the structural differences between GFL and GFM, there are differences in their harmonic outputs and responses. In this paper, the differences in the effects of control parameters, dead time, and background harmonics on the grid-connected current harmonics of GFL and GFM are analyzed. Finally, through a data-driven analysis, the simulation results validate the proposed harmonic performance differences between GFL and GFM.

articleTitle: Distributed Voltage Control Strategy for High Proportion Photovoltaic Distribution Network Considering Abnormal Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The distributed reactive power coordinated control of photovoltaic inverter group has the potential to solve the problems of serious voltage over-limit and voltage fluctuation. The effectiveness of the distributed voltage control strategy currently studied is based on the premise of perfect communication. However, the actual distribution network has abnormal communication conditions such as random delay, error code, packet loss, network attack and network congestion, resulting in unsatisfactory voltage control effect. In order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes a distributed voltage control strategy for distribution network considering communication anomalies. The strategy solves the problems of communication data delay, packet loss and attack by constructing asynchronous iterative architecture, information retransmission and information verification. Through the IEEE 33 node example, it is verified that the method proposed in this paper can effectively solve the influence of abnormal communication in distribution network on voltage control effect.

articleTitle: Multi-pulse Active Substation for Power Quality Improvement and Recuperation of Regenerative Braking Energy in DC Railway
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of active traction substations (ATSS) equipped with interleaved PWM rectifiers to enhance regenerative braking energy (RBE) utilization in bidirectional power systems. By comparing modern ATSS with conventional diode-bridge rectifier traction power substation (TPSS) in a bilateral DC railway setup, the study utilizes the operational context of the Italian 3 kV DC railway line as a case study. Various power quality parameters are analyzed to determine the optimal design, including overhead contact line voltage fluctuation, stress on passive components, total harmonic distortion in primary side of TPSS, voltage and current imbalances, and power factor. Real-world data from the Italian railway system ensures the relevance and accuracy of the findings, providing valuable insights for the implementation of ATSS in similar railway infrastructures.

articleTitle: Review of revisions of IEEE 519 Standard on Power System Harmonics (1981 to 2022)
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Harmonics is one of the important Power Quality disturbances and recently IEEE published 519-2022 standard which defines the limits of harmonic distortion in power systems. It is observed that after three revisions, the 519 standard is still misunderstood and consequently erroneously interpreted and applied in a few cases, especially in developing countries. The challenges faced are calculating Isc, confusion in applying the 99<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 95<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> percentiles and understanding even harmonics and multipliers. This paper reviews the revisions of IEEE 519 since its inception in 1981 and the major changes in 2014 and 2022 versions. This will help users clearly understand the philosophy of the standard and the correct interpretation and implementation of the standard in practice. A few suggestions, such as the inclusion of case studies, harmonic limits at equipment terminals, the possibility of inclusion of supra harmonics, etc., in the next revision of the IEEE 519 standard are discussed.

articleTitle: Review of Power Quality Standard System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the continuous increase of sensitive loads in the power grid, users have increasingly higher requirements for power quality. The research and practice of power quality are increasingly valued by scholars and the industry. Correspondingly, the relevant standards for power quality are also showing an increasingly rich trend. Personnel engaged in the power quality industry often have difficulty in having a comprehensive and systematic understanding of power quality standards. To solve this problem, we proposed an overview of the existing power quality standards. We firstly classify them according to organizations, such as IEEE, IEC and SAC. On this basis, various standards issued by each standardization organization are classified and discussed according to the content involved. Finally we briefly describe the content and the involved areas of the standard. This review is hoped to be helpful for related research and application.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Method for County-level Distribution Network Considering Multi-function Reuse of Mobile Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In the context of the carbon neutrality goal and the rising penetration of renewable energies, the electrical power system’s dependency on renewable energy sources, including photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation, has markedly increased. However, the generation of renewable energy is heavily dependent on climatic conditions, and its volatility can bring pressure to the power balance of the distribution network. The application of mobile energy storage system (MESS) will become a strong support for the extensive expansion of renewable energy sources. Hence, an optimal scheduling method for county-level distribution networks (CDNs) considering the multi-function reuse of MESS is proposed. Firstly, the application scenarios and necessity of multi-function reuse of MESS under the context of a significant share of renewable energy sources are analyzed. Then, an optimal scheduling method considering MESS is constructed, aiming at reducing the overall operating expenses of the CDN, as well as the constraints such as the spatiotemporal dynamic scheduling of MESS. Finally, a revised 33-bus distribution network is applied for case studies. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model is applicable to different scenarios of the CDN under various application functions of MESS, effectively reducing the operational costs of the CDN and ensuring the power supply for load demand.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Distribution Network Substitutive Energy Storage for Economic Operation and Renewable Energy Accommodation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: With the growing share of renewable energy sources (RES), configuring substitutive energy storag system (SESS) in distribution networks to mitigate the fluctuations of renewable energy hold significant importance. To this end, an optimal approach for configuring substitutive energy storage is proposed in this paper, aimed at the cost-effective operation of the distribution system and the accommodation of renewable energy. Firstly, a collaborative operation model of SESS in distribution networks and user-side energy storage is constructed, and the operation mode of SESS in the distribution network is analyzed. Then, with the minimization of the distribution network planning and operation cost as the objective function, an optimization model for the siting and sizing of SESS in the distribution network is established to achieve energy storage planning. On this basis, based on stochastic programming to represent the uncertainty in wind and solar power generation, the configuration model is linearized using a penalty factor method. Finally, case studies are conducted on the modified 33-nodes distribution network to confirm the proposed method's effectiveness and practicality.

articleTitle: Optimization Configuration Method for Harmonic Monitoring in Local Distribution Networks for Global Harmonics Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The increase of nonlinear loads in distribution networks has led to a more serious harmonic issue and an increasing demand for monitoring and mitigation. The traditional configuration of monitoring and control equipment requires access to numerous devices, resulting in low efficiency and high costs. Aiming at global harmonic improvement, this article presents an optimal configuration method for harmonic monitoring devices. Firstly, the topology connectivity model is established based on the network topology for harmonic state estimation and observability analysis. Subsequently, the ant colony algorithm is adapted to determine the quantity and position of monitoring devices. Based on the optimal configuration result of harmonic monitoring devices, an improved multi-objective ant colony algorithm is proposed to solve the configuration of active power filters (APFs) to achieve global harmonic improvement. Then, an IEEE-18 bus test system that incorporates nonlinear loads is conducted in simulation. After configuring harmonic monitoring devices and APFs according to the results, the harmonic distortion in the distribution network can meet the recommended standard.

articleTitle: Renewable Scenario Generation Under Extreme Meteorological Conditions via Improved Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Scenario generation is a crucial method for characterizing the uncertainty of renewable energy sources (RESs). Driven by climate change, more frequent extreme meteorological events complicate the uncertainty of RESs and challenge the safe operation of high-penetrated renewable power systems. In response, this paper proposes an improved Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGANs) approach to address generate renewable scenarios under extreme meteorological conditions. Firstly, the problem of renewable scenario generation under extreme meteorological conditions and the encoding rules for meteorological conditions are established. Subsequently, the Wasserstein distance and gradient penalty are employed to refine the CGAN, and a novel class and weight assignment method is devised to tackle the scenario class imbalance and capture fluctuations in renewable power generation. Case studies conducted on an open-source dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach can generate corresponding scenarios under given conditions and effectively imitate the distribution of historical scenarios.
